About Us

At Red Fox Remodeling, we believe your home should be designed around the way you live. As a locally owned and operated remodeling company serving the Twin Cities, we specialize in creating thoughtful, beautifully crafted spaces that feel as functional as they are inviting.

​

Whether it's a kitchen where family gathers, a bathroom that offers a daily retreat, or a whole-home transformation, we approach every project with care, clear communication, and a commitment to quality. Our team works closely with homeowners from the first conversation through the final walkthrough, ensuring every detail reflects your vision and lifestyle.

​

We take pride in delivering exceptional craftsmanship, using premium materials, and building lasting relationships with the families we serve. For us, remodeling is about more than improving homes, it's about creating spaces where life's best moments unfold.

Meet Your Team
Denny Meints

Owner + Operations

Denny Meints is the founder of Red Fox Remodeling. He started the company in 2022 after years of experience in home remodeling and construction management. Denny built Red Fox around integrity, transparent pricing, and quality craftsmanship. Today, he leads a team serving Twin Cities homeowners and transforming houses into homes.

Asher Webb

Project Manager

Asher has worked in building and remodeling industry for over a decade, including five years in executive-level project management. He brings knowledge of the building process, trade management, and client success. His track record and expertise help ensure homeowners receive guidance and a remodeling experience from start to finish.

Wade Kyllonen

Site Supervisor

Wade has spent over 14 years in the remodeling industry, serving clients in the Twin Cities area. He brings a steady presence to job sites and takes pride in keeping projects on time, on budget, and moving smoothly. His experience makes him a great part of the team. Outside of work, Wade enjoys spending time with his family and exploring the outdoors.

Evan Wrazidlo

Carpenter

Evan joins Red Fox as an carpenter, craftsman, and laborer with a passion for quality workmanship. His attention to detail, work ethic, and commitment to construction make him a valuable asset to the team. Evan takes pride in delivering craftsmanship that helps bring each remodeling project to life.

Chad Torp

Construction Estimator

Chad has over 10 years of experience in remodeling as a carpenter, project manager, and construction estimator. He enjoys preparing clients and projects for a successful start and brings a thoughtful, detail-oriented approach to every project. Outside of work, Chad enjoys spending time with his family, hiking, camping, and exploring the outdoors.

Mai See Thao

Lead Designer

Mai See Thao is an interior designer with 7 years of experience creating spaces. She enjoys collaborating with clients to design homes that reflect their lifestyles and personalities. Outside of work, Mai See loves hiking with her dogs, playing pickleball, and hosting friends. She values relationships with clients and partners.

Graycen Mourhess

Junior Designer

Graycen is a Junior Designer who earned her degree in Interior Design and is excited to begin her remodeling career. She is passionate about creating beautiful, functional spaces that reflect client's style and needs. Graycen enjoys collaborating with clients, bringing ideas to projects, and continuously learning while developing design solutions.

Your Dream Kitchen Built For Your Family

Experience quality craftsmanship with award-winning kitchen remodelers.

Book Your Consultation
Time for a renovation?

We transform kitchens into beautiful, functional spaces that fit your lifestyle. With expert craftsmanship, attention to detail, and a commitment to quality, we deliver remodels that not only look amazing but stand the test of time.

Kitchens Starting at $75k

With every project thoughtfully designed around your vision, needs, and investment. We provide transparent pricing throughout the process, so you always know where your project stands from start to finish.

Increased property value
Modern and customized space
Improved functionality
Fast and efficient build timeline
Entertainment-ready space
Here's how it works:

We turn your vision into reality with transparency, quality assurance, and customer satisfaction at every step.

1. Discovery & Design

We learn about your vision and budget, create your initial design and estimate, and finalize your project direction through a collaborative design and approval process.

2. Prepare & Plan

Our team handles permits, coordinates partners, and sources all materials to ensure everything is ready before construction begins.

3. Build & Celebrate

We bring your project to life with clear communication, walkthroughs, and final touch-ups before celebrating your beautifully finished space.

Frequently Asked Questions
How much will our project cost?

Every kitchen remodel is unique, and the final investment depends on the scope, design, materials, and selections involved. As a general guide, kitchen remodels typically range from $90,000 to $200,000, with projects starting around $75,000 for a more basic scope.

How long does a typical kitchen remodel take?

Most full kitchen remodels take 10 weeks of construction, depending on scope. The entire process including design, selections, permits, and ordering materials often takes 6-8 months from first consultation to completion.

Can I live in my home during the remodel?

In most cases, yes, you can continue to live in your home. You may need to move out of your home for a portion of a kitchen remodel depending on the scope of the project.

How far in advance should I start planning?

Ideally, 3-6 months before you want construction to begin. Custom cabinetry and specialty materials can have long lead times and it's important to leave time for a full custom design process.

Is it better to add on to a home or finish existing space like a basement or attic?

We can't say one is better than the other, but utilizing existing space can be a more economical way to gain living space in your home. However, there are plenty of reasons an addition will be a better project to achieve the goals you have for your home!

Do you allow homeowners to contract you for 'partial projects' like only the structural elements?

We will consider a partial project, but there needs to be clear scope delineation from day one and we cannot hand off any work that requires a city inspection connected to our permit.

What is a reasonable timeline to expect our addition to be completed in?

Every timeline is unique to the specific project scope, but generally we'll need nine to twelve weeks to design your new space, four to six weeks for project preparations and the build may take anywhere from four to eight months depending on size and scope.

Are you ready for a space you're proud of?

A whole-home remodel gives you the opportunity to completely reimagine the space you already love. From updated layouts and modern finishes to improved functionality and timeless design, we bring every room together into a home that feels beautifully and uniquely yours.

Whole Home Remodels Starting at $350k

For a complete transformation, we thoughtfully reimagine every space in your home to create a cohesive design that fits the way you live. From major structural changes to the finishing details, our team brings your vision to life from start to finish.

Increased property value

Here's how it works

We turn your vision into reality with transparency, quality assurance, and customer satisfaction at every step.

1. Discovery & Design

We learn about your vision and budget, create your initial design and estimate, and finalize your project direction through a collaborative design and approval process.

2. Prepare & Plan

Our team handles permits, coordinates partners, and sources all materials to ensure everything is ready before construction begins.

3. Build & Celebrate

We bring your project to life with clear communication, walkthroughs, and final touch-ups before celebrating your beautifully finished space.

Frequently Asked Questions
Do we have to move out during our remodel?

For a whole-home renovation, you'll likely need to relocate for at least part of the project. Depending on the scope and duration of the project, it may be best if your family moves out of the home completely. This will actually shorten the overall project duration and be more tolerable for you!

If we're looking for a home in a particular neighborhood, can you get us remodel estimates before we purchase?

Yes, if you involve us early in your home search process we can give you general price guidance on specific properties and scopes of work.

Generally, how long does a whole home remodel take?

This can be hard to answer because every remodeling scope is different. If there are no structural changes or additions involved, your project may be done as quickly as four or five months, however for more complicated or comprehensive remodels, timelines can increase up to eight or nine months.

At what point does it make sense to tear down and rebuild instead of taking on a whole home remodel?

A full tear-down can make sense in several situations. (1) The property is in a perfect location with a perfect lot, but the home itself is too small or generally doesn't meet your needs. (2) If there are known structural or health concerns including water damage, mold, or sinking foundations. (3) If your home has experienced a disaster such as fire or flood, it can lend a unique opportunity to start completely fresh with a new layout and functionality for life.

Build the house of your dreams

From design to final inspection our team handles everything. So your custom home build is stress-free.

Start Your Free Consultation
Are you ready for a home you're proud of?

Building a custom home is an opportunity to create a space that is truly designed around the way you live. From the initial vision to the final details, Red Fox Remodeling brings thoughtful design, quality craftsmanship, and a personalized approach to creating a home that is uniquely yours.

Custom Builds Starting at $350k

A custom home can be designed around your lifestyle, your family, and the details that matter most to you. Red Fox Remodeling combines thoughtful planning and quality craftsmanship to help bring your vision to life from the ground up.

Personalized design
No compromising on layout
Built for the future in mind
Modern efficiency & technology
Quality craftsmanship
Here's how it works

We turn your vision into reality with transparency, quality assurance, and customer satisfaction at every step.

1. Discovery & Design

We learn about your vision and budget, create your initial design and estimate, and finalize your project direction through a collaborative design and approval process.

2. Prepare & Plan

Our team handles permits, coordinates partners, and sources all materials to ensure everything is ready before construction begins.

3. Build & Celebrate

We bring your project to life with clear communication, walkthroughs, and final touch-ups before celebrating your beautifully finished space.

Frequently Asked Questions
Do you have a number of set home plans to pick from or do you design from scratch?

We design every home project from the ground up. A custom home is a unique opportunity to leverage every inch of your home to conform to how you want to live. 

Why is a custom home so much more expensive than a new home in a development?

Economies of scale and simplicity of designs. Developers can sell homes for hundreds of thousands less per home because they sell hundreds of homes in a year. Beyond that, generally speaking, homes built by developers take few risks, are simple to construct and use a set number of floor plans. Custom homes are 100% bespoke, include unique and inspiring features, and will only be built once - all those differentiators drive price, but also drive incredible results!

Do you have lots available for building?

We do not currently offer lots for customers to build on. We require custom build customers to secure their own buildable lot and confirm the ability to build with the proper local authorities before purchasing. 

How long does a custom build take from start of design to finish?

Typically a truly custom home will take over a year from the start of design to final inspection. Four to six months are spent locking in the design, with the next eight to ten months spent building the home.

Frequently Asked Questions
How much will our project cost?

So many factors go into the final construction bid that there is truly no one-size fits all' answer here. However, a bathroom remodel typically ranges from $65,000 to $150,000.

How long does a bathroom remodel take?

A bathroom remodel typically takes 6–8 weeks of construction. Larger primary bathrooms with layout changes, custom tile, or specialty materials can take longer.

Can I live in my home during the remodel?

In most cases, yes, you can continue to live in your home. If your home has more than one bathroom, you can continue living there throughout the project.

How far in advance should I start planning?

Ideally, 3–6 months before you want construction to begin. Specialty materials can have long lead times and it's important to leave time for a full custom design process.

Here's How it Works.

We turn your vision into reality with transparency, quality assurance, and customer satisfaction at every step.

1. Discovery & Design

We learn about your vision and budget, create your initial design and estimate, and finalize your project direction through a collaborative design and approval process.

2. Prepare & Plan

Our team handles permits, coordinates partners, and sources all materials to ensure everything is ready before construction begins.

3. Build & Celebrate

We bring your project to life with clear communication, walkthroughs, and final touch-ups before celebrating your beautifully finished space.

Frequently Asked Questions
How much will our project cost?

So many factors go into the final construction bid that there is truly no 'one size fits all' answer here. However, for a full basement remodel which includes a bathroom, bedroom and living space, we tend to see project costs around $100,000. 

How long will this project take?

Designing your space with you and making all material selections can take 1-2 months. Once we've finalized the design, the construction phase will be 3-4 months depending on features you've selected and complexity of the project.

How soon can you start our project?

Design can always always start immediately, but our construction start times vary depending on the scope of the work. Typically you could expect to start your project within 4-5 months of signing your design contract.

Do I need drain tile and a sump pump before finishing my basement?

Drain tile is a building system designed to keep groundwater out of your basement and protects your interior finishes (think drywall, carpet, etc). Not every home needs a drain tile system due to water table depth, soil composition, and history of the home - however, this is something we can evaluate with you during the design process.

Do you remediate mold or asbestos issues?

No. We are not an abatement company which are specifically licensed to remove mold, asbestos or other harmful material. However, not all situations require abatement. We can encapsulate asbestos material (leave it in place and install a new product over the top) and many mold problems never rise to the level of needing professional abatement help.

Executive Craftsman

St. Paul

Kitchen • Bathrooms • Primary Bedroom

This young family loved their historic St. Paul home and the character of their established neighborhood, but their growing family had quickly outgrown the home’s compact footprint. With the dining room doubling as overflow kitchen space, no main-level bathroom, and no connection to the backyard, they needed more room without giving up the home and community they loved.
The Client's Needs

The goal was to create a home that felt spacious, functional, and welcoming for the entire family while preserving the historic character that made the original home so special.

Our Design Priorities
1
Expand Without Losing Character

Create a thoughtful addition that feels original to the home by carrying its historic materials, details, and proportions throughout the new spaces.

2
Create Space for Everyone

Give the family dedicated places to cook, gather, work, and relax while creating a better sense of connection between the kitchen, backyard, and rest of the home.

3
Make Every Square Foot Count

Use intentional layouts and carefully selected details to add meaningful function. Even within the home’s smallest spaces.

Kitchen

The new kitchen was designed around the way the family actually lives, with both an island and peninsula providing distinct areas for food preparation, homework, gathering, and everyday seating. A new sliding door creates direct access to the backyard and patio, while hardwood flooring and custom millwork were carefully matched to the original home so the new space feels as though it has always been there.

Half Bathroom

Though the footprint was exceptionally small, the new main-level powder room proves that a compact space can still have plenty of character. Heated floors, wainscoting, and a refined wall-mounted sink make this practical addition feel polished and intentional while giving the family a much-needed bathroom for everyday life and entertaining.

Primary Suite

Upstairs, the new primary suite provides the family with a dedicated retreat, including a sophisticated full bathroom designed for both beauty and improved function. Real marble flooring, an elevated herringbone shower, a reconfigured vanity and toilet layout, and added linen storage turn the compact space into a thoughtful and luxurious upgrade.

Exterior Addition

The rear addition was carefully designed to disappear into the original architecture of the home. Matching the existing siding, windows, and roofing materials created a seamless transition, while the new connection to the patio finally gave the family the backyard access they had been missing.

A note from the owner,

"This was one of those projects where we genuinely loved the people as much as we loved the work. The family was so much fun to work with, and it was incredibly rewarding to help them create a home that could truly accommodate everyone while still honoring the history of the house. We especially loved the challenge of carrying the original home’s historic details into every part of the addition. Most of all, it was exciting to see this family gain the space and functionality they needed without having to leave the home and neighborhood they loved."

​

- Denny Meints

Sophisticated  Living

St. Paul

Kitchen • Bathrooms • Primary Bedroom

This young family loved their St. Paul neighborhood and historic home, but over time, the spaces at the heart of their daily life no longer felt like a reflection of their family or their personal style. With growing children and a desire to stay in their home for years to come, they wanted to create spaces that felt elevated and beautiful while also working better for the way their family actually lived.
The Client's Needs

The goal was to refresh the home’s most-used spaces with a sophisticated, timeless aesthetic while adding practical function for a growing family and honoring the character of the historic home.

Our Design Priorities
1
Elevate the Everyday

Transform the kitchen and bathrooms into beautiful, intentional spaces using natural, high-quality materials that would feel special every day and stand the test of time.

2
Design for Family Life

Improve the function of the home with thoughtful storage, flexible bathing spaces, and layouts that allow multiple family members to use the spaces comfortably at once.

3
Honor the Character

Create a cohesive aesthetic that feels appropriate to the historic house while introducing the family’s more refined, sophisticated style throughout the spaces.

Kitchen

The kitchen became a true focal point of the home with custom walnut cabinetry, polished brass hardware, a solid marble countertop, and a classic farmhouse sink. While the existing layout did not require major functional changes, the transformation of the materials and finishes completely elevated the space, giving the family a kitchen that felt distinctly their own and built to last.

Basement Bathroom

Designed with a more masculine aesthetic for the husband, this basement bathroom balances deep, high-contrast finishes with lighter elements that help brighten the naturally darker space. Brass accents, distinctive floor tile, and added storage give the room both personality and practicality, creating a space that works especially well as a post-workout retreat.

Family Bathroom

The main family bathroom was designed around the realities of life with children, with a dedicated wet room that places the tub and shower together behind glass for contained, easy-to-manage bathing. A curved wall subtly conceals the shower while adding an architectural element, while the combination of a darker wood vanity, marble, brass, and soft finishes creates a timeless and sophisticated look.

A note from the owner,

"What I loved most about this project was that we were able to touch every level of the home and make a meaningful difference in the way this family lives. From the basement bathroom to the main family spaces, every improvement was connected to making their home more functional, more beautiful, and more reflective of who they are. I especially enjoyed finding that balance between sophisticated design and the realities of raising a family, because the spaces still needed to work hard every day. They were also such genuinely kind people to work with, which made the entire project that much more rewarding."

​

- Denny Meints

Garden Cottage 

St. Paul

Kitchen • Bathroom • Dining

This growing St. Paul family loved the history and charm of their home, but a poorly executed renovation in the 1990s had left many of its spaces feeling disconnected, dated, and in need of repair. With a third child on the way and a love for hosting family and friends, they knew it was time to restore the home’s character while making it work better for the life they were building there.
The Client's Needs

The goal was to bring the historic home back to its original character while improving functionality, increasing storage and natural light, and creating a better connection to the garden and outdoors.

Our Design Priorities
1
Restore Historic Character

Reintroduce thoughtful materials, millwork, and architectural details that feel authentic to the home and restore the charm that had been lost over time.

2
Utilize Small Spaces

Reconfigure tight and unconventional spaces with creative layouts, custom features, and purposeful storage so every square foot could serve the family well.

3
Bring the Outdoors In

Increase natural light and strengthen the connection to the family’s beloved garden through new windows, thoughtful sightlines, and nature-inspired colors and materials.

Kitchen

The kitchen was completely reimagined with custom cabinetry, butcher block countertops, brick flooring, handmade backsplash tile, and brass hardware that reinforce the home’s historic character. The layout was carefully rearranged to better accommodate the appliances and daily workflow, while custom features, including a concealed coffee bar behind French-style doors and a hidden bookshelf that opens to reveal basement access, add layers of personality and surprise.

Dining Room

Because hosting was such an important part of this family’s life, the dining room was designed to provide flexibility between everyday living and entertaining. A widened opening with custom doors allows the dining room to open up when they need more gathering space or close off when desired, with custom trim and millwork carefully matched to the historic character of the home.

Bathroom

Working within an exceptionally tight footprint, the bathroom required a creative approach to make every inch functional. A tucked-away vanity, pocket door, wall-mounted toilet, and wet-room configuration allow the shower and toilet to share the compact space, while green tile, a mirrored pocket door, and a window within the shower bring in personality and natural light.

A note from the owner,

"What I loved most about this project was all of the little details that made the home feel completely unique to this family. The hidden basement door, concealed coffee bar, beautiful green accents, and thoughtful connection to their garden each added something special without taking away from the home’s historic character. I especially loved how we were able to bring more natural light and the family’s love of plants into the design, creating spaces that feel both charming and connected to the outdoors. In the end, the home became cozy, functional, and full of character. A place this family can enjoy and cherish for generations."

​

- Denny Meints

Emerald Retreat

St. Paul

Bathroom • Laundry

This family loved their beautiful historic neighborhood and had no desire to leave, but their home’s existing layout created one major everyday frustration: doing laundry meant traveling nearly two full stories. Their primary bathroom also needed a thoughtful update, creating an opportunity to solve the laundry challenge while transforming the space into a bright, elevated retreat that felt worthy of the historic home.
The Client's Needs

The goal was to modernize the primary bathroom, introduce convenient laundry without sacrificing the room’s character, and make the challenging pitched-ceiling layout feel intentional, bright, and luxurious.

Our Design Priorities
1
Maximize Every Inch

Use every inch of the unusual pitched-ceiling footprint to accommodate both a beautiful bathroom and a concealed laundry area without compromising the room’s flow.

2
Bring in Natural Light

Take advantage of the roofline with a strategically placed skylight and integrated lighting to make the space feel open, bright, and connected to the outdoors.

3
Create an Timeless Space

Use classic materials, thoughtful proportions, and refined details to create a bathroom that feels elevated today and beautiful for years to come.

Bathroom & Laundry

The pitched ceiling became an opportunity rather than a limitation, allowing the walk-in shower to tuck naturally beneath the slope with adding a beautiful skylight positioned directly above it. Emerald green tile, marble flooring, heated floors, and integrated lighting around the skylight create a sophisticated, spa-like atmosphere, while the laundry unit is cleverly concealed behind custom French-style cabinetry beside the shower. The cabinetry was crafted by the client’s father, adding an incredibly personal layer of craftsmanship and creating a meaningful heirloom element within the space.

A note from the owner,

"One of my favorite things about this project is how the natural light completely changes the experience of the room. It almost feels like a luxurious treehouse. The skylight, emerald tile, and connection to the outdoors make it such a unique and peaceful space, while the hidden laundry adds an incredible amount of everyday function. But what makes this project especially meaningful is the cabinetry made by the client’s father; knowing that his craftsmanship will remain in the home as an heirloom piece for the family makes the space feel so much more personal. It was incredibly rewarding to take a challenging layout and turn it into something beautiful, functional, and deeply connected to the people who live there."

​

- Denny Meints

KITCHEN REMODELING IN ROSEVILLE & THE SACRAMENTO AREA
We've Seen a Lot of Kitchens.
Yours Can Be Better.

There's a difference between a kitchen that looks nice in photos and one that actually works. We've been remodeling kitchens in Roseville, Sacramento and the surrounding suburbs long enough to know that most homeowners don't want magazine-perfect — they want a space where cooking doesn't feel like a battle with the floor plan.

Whether it's a full kitchen renovation with a new layout, flooring and everything in between — or targeted upgrades to the two or three things that bother you daily — we handle both. Our office is on Lava Ridge Court in Roseville, so site visits, sample reviews and inspection days are coordinated by people who work locally, not a franchise crew dispatched from hours away. Cabinets are often the biggest decision in the room, so many full remodels include custom cabinetry built to your kitchen's dimensions, and if the bathroom is next on your list, see our bathroom remodeling work.

We work across Roseville, Granite Bay, Rocklin, Folsom, El Dorado Hills, Fair Oaks and Sacramento. If you have a vague idea or a detailed plan, either works. Browse recent projects in our gallery, read how we work, then request a free in-home estimate.

REQUEST YOUR FREE ESTIMATE

WHAT WE BRING TO EVERY KITCHEN PROJECT

OUR KITCHEN REMODELING SERVICES
Full Remodels, Focused Upgrades,
Everything In Between

We don't do one-size-fits-all. Some homeowners want to gut the whole kitchen and start fresh. Others just need the layout fixed or the cabinets swapped. Both are projects we take seriously.

MOST COMMON
Full Kitchen Remodel

A full remodel means rethinking everything — layout, plumbing, electrical, flooring, cabinets, countertops, lighting, appliances. It's the most common project we take on in the Roseville and Sacramento area. It takes longer and costs more up front, but the result is a kitchen that works the way your family actually cooks and lives.

We'll walk you through what's realistic for your budget, what to prioritize, and what can wait. No pressure, no overselling. For planning numbers, see what a kitchen remodel costs in our area.

TALK ABOUT YOUR FULL REMODEL
Layout redesign
Plumbing & electrical
Custom cabinetry
Countertops
Flooring
Lighting
Appliance coordination
Permit coordination
HIGH IMPACT
Targeted Upgrades

Not every project needs to be a full gut. Sometimes the issue is bad counter space, a kitchen with no light, or a fridge in the wrong place. Done right, targeted upgrades change how a kitchen feels — and if the boxes are solid, cabinet refacing can transform the room for less than full custom cabinetry. Getting ready to sell? Our guide on what's worth remodeling before you sell helps you decide how far to go.

Countertop replacement
New flooring
Backsplash
Cabinet refacing
Lighting updates
Hardware refresh
STRUCTURAL THINKING
Layout & Flow Changes

Older homes especially tend to have kitchens designed for a different era — walls that don't need to be there, doorways in strange places. If your kitchen is functionally awkward, we help identify what may be structural, bring in a qualified engineer when needed, and price what it would take to change. Considering removing a wall? Our guide on open-concept kitchen conversions covers what's involved and what it costs.

Wall removal
Open-concept conversion
Island addition
Traffic flow redesign
Pantry creation
KITCHEN REMODEL COST
What a Kitchen Remodel Costs in
Roseville & Sacramento

Nobody likes "it depends," so here are the planning ranges we typically see across the Roseville and greater Sacramento market. They're a starting point for budgeting — not a fixed quote. Your number comes in writing, line by line, after we've seen the kitchen.

COSMETIC REFRESH
$25,000 – $45,000

Same footprint. New countertops, backsplash, flooring, lighting, hardware and paint, often with cabinets refaced rather than replaced.

MID-RANGE FULL REMODEL
$50,000 – $90,000

New cabinets, stone counters, appliances, flooring and updated plumbing and electrical, sometimes with modest layout changes.

HIGH-END RENOVATION
$100,000+

Full custom cabinetry, wall removal or relocated plumbing, premium appliance packages, specialty stone and layered lighting design.

Planning estimates only. Actual pricing depends on scope, materials, site conditions and permit requirements.

What moves the number

A handful of decisions account for most of the spread between a refresh and a full custom kitchen. For a deeper breakdown, read our guide to what a kitchen remodel actually costs in Sacramento.

Prefer to spread the cost out? See our financing options (subject to lender approval), or request a free in-home estimate. We're also happy to phase a project.

1
Cabinets
Often the largest single line item. Stock, semi-custom and built-to-order cabinetry can differ widely in price for the same kitchen.
2
Whether plumbing, gas or walls move
Keeping the sink and range in place saves money. Moving them, or removing a wall, means new rough-in, possible structural work and more inspections.
3
Countertops and appliances
Quartz, granite, quartzite and butcher block differ in price and upkeep, and appliance packages range from standard to professional-grade.
4
What's behind the drywall
Older homes can reveal outdated wiring, galvanized supply lines or subfloor damage. We include a contingency rather than assume it won't happen.
HOW A KITCHEN REMODEL UNFOLDS
The Timeline,
Honestly

Most of the waiting in a kitchen remodel happens before anyone swings a hammer. Here's how the schedule commonly breaks down for a full remodel — typical ranges, not guarantees.

2–4
WEEKS
Design & planning

In-home visit, measurements, layout options, selections and a written, line-by-line quote. The cheapest stage to change your mind.

2–6
WEEKS
Permit review

Depends on the jurisdiction and project scope. Usually runs alongside cabinet ordering rather than after it.

4–10
WEEKS
Cabinet lead time

Often the longest single wait. We aim to schedule demolition around confirmed delivery so the kitchen isn't gutted while you wait.

4–8
WEEKS ON SITE
Construction

Demo, rough plumbing and electrical, inspections, drywall, flooring, cabinets, countertop templating, backsplash, fixtures and punch list.

3–5 months
TYPICAL TOTAL

Because permits and cabinet orders usually overlap with planning, the total from first meeting to cooking again often lands around three to five months. Inspection scheduling, material deliveries, design changes and what turns up behind older walls can all shift it. Roughly four to eight of those weeks are when the kitchen is out of service — plan a temporary setup with a microwave, small fridge and coffee station in another room, and we'll flag the most disruptive days in advance.

PERMITS & CODE
Permits, Inspections
and Why They Matter

We prepare permit applications, coordinate plan submission and schedule inspections on every project that needs them.

In California, kitchen work that changes plumbing, electrical or structure generally needs a permit — which covers most full remodels. Adding circuits for an island, relocating a sink or taking out a wall all trigger review; a straight countertop swap often doesn't. Each building department sets its own requirements and review times, so we plan the schedule around the office that has jurisdiction over your address.

California's energy code (Title 24) includes lighting requirements for kitchen remodels, so we plan fixtures and controls with that in mind from the start. Other electrical work follows the applicable electrical code and the inspector's review.

Permits matter beyond paperwork: unpermitted work can surface during a sale, an appraisal or an insurance claim. A permitted remodel is documented work on a documented house.

CUSTOM KITCHEN RENOVATION
Designed Around
How You Actually Cook

Every household cooks differently. Some people need tons of counter space. Others prioritize storage. Some want a big island for the kids to sit at. Others just need a layout where two people can be in the kitchen at once without bumping into each other.

A custom kitchen renovation starts with that conversation — not with a showroom catalog. We want to know how your kitchen fails you right now, before we talk about what it could look like. We'll tell you when something costs more than it's worth, and when spending a little extra will make a real difference.

1
In-home consultation
We come to you, see the space, and talk through what you want to change and why.
2
Design & planning
We map out layout options, material choices, and a realistic scope based on your budget.
3
Build & finish
Work follows an agreed schedule, with one contact for questions throughout.

See more finished kitchens in our project gallery.

PLANNING YOUR KITCHEN
The Decisions That
Shape the Result

A good kitchen is mostly the sum of a handful of choices. These are the ones we spend the most time on with homeowners.

Layout and Clearances

Before style, we look at how you move. Design guidelines such as those from the National Kitchen & Bath Association suggest about 42 inches between counters for one cook and 48 inches when two cook together. These are planning guidelines, not code minimums, but an island that crowds the walkways will annoy you every day, so we check the numbers against your actual room. Taking out a wall? Read our guide to open-concept kitchen conversions first.

Cabinets: Replace, Reface or Build Custom

Refacing can make sense when the boxes are solid and the layout stays put. When the layout changes or the boxes are worn, replacing them is usually the better value. Odd wall lengths, tall ceilings and pantry needs are where custom cabinetry earns its cost. We'll show you the trade-offs without steering you to the most expensive option.

Countertops and Surfaces

Quartz, granite, quartzite and butcher block all work; they differ mainly in upkeep, edge details and price. Take a large sample home and look at it in morning and evening light next to your cabinet finish before committing. Flooring and backsplash go the same way — it's much cheaper to change your mind on a sample than on an installed slab.

Lighting, Electrical and Plumbing

Most kitchens are under-lit, and layered lighting — ceiling, task and under-cabinet — changes the room more than almost any finish. Title 24 sets lighting requirements for kitchen remodels, which we plan for from the start. With walls open, it's the right time to add outlets, move a sink or replace old supply lines. Older homes sometimes need a panel upgrade for modern appliances, and we aim to flag that in the estimate rather than mid-project.

WHERE WE REMODEL KITCHENS
Based in Roseville,
Building Across the Region

Every part of the Sacramento region has its own kinds of houses, and that changes what a kitchen remodel looks like.

Roseville & Rocklin

Our office is in Roseville. Many homes here and in Rocklin were built from the 1990s through the 2010s in planned communities — sound structure, but builder-grade kitchens with tile counters, soffits and closed peninsulas. Rocklin also mixes an older downtown core with neighborhoods like Whitney Ranch and Stanford Ranch. See Roseville and Rocklin.

Granite Bay & El Dorado Hills

Larger homes where projects often lean toward custom cabinetry, bigger islands, better stone and appliance packages that need dedicated circuits and real ventilation planning. Some communities have architectural review for exterior changes. See Granite Bay and El Dorado Hills.

Sacramento

Craftsman homes and bungalows in Land Park, Curtis Park, Midtown, the Fab 40s and East Sacramento, plus mid-century ranches farther out. In older houses, wiring and drain lines can need attention once walls open, which is why we price from a written estimate after seeing the house. More on our Sacramento page.

Folsom & Fair Oaks

From newer builds in Folsom to established neighborhoods in Fair Oaks with character worth keeping and systems worth updating. We plan for what older construction may reveal rather than writing an optimistic number.

The Kind of Kitchen Remodel

When you search for kitchen remodeling near me, you get a lot of results. Here's what makes working with us actually different.

A Bathroom That Finally Works

Most homeowners put off a bathroom remodel longer than they should. It's disruptive, it's not cheap, and there are a lot of contractors out there who make the process harder than it needs to be.

We get it. That's why our bathroom remodeling services are built around clear communication, honest pricing, and showing up when we say we will. No disappearing acts. No vague timelines. No surprise invoices.

Whether you're updating a dated guest bath or tackling a full bathroom remodel on your primary suite, we'll help you figure out what makes sense for your space and your budget — and we'll be upfront if something isn't worth the cost.

WHAT WE DO

We don't have a standard package we slot everyone into. Here's what we typically help homeowners with — and how we approach each one.

MOST POPULAR
Complete Bathroom Remodeling

A full bathroom remodel means starting fresh — new layout if needed, new plumbing, new tile, new fixtures, new everything. Complete bathroom remodeling is the right move when things are too far gone for partial fixes, or when you've been dreaming about something completely different.

We plan it carefully so nothing gets missed and nothing surprises you mid-project. You'll know exactly what's happening and when, from the first day to the last.

START PLANNING YOUR FULL REMODEL

HIGH IMPACT
Shower Remodel

The shower is often the biggest pain point. Outdated surrounds, cramped dimensions, grout that's beyond saving. A shower remodel can mean anything from swapping out the surround and fixtures to a full walk-in conversion. We'll tell you exactly what's involved before you commit to anything.

Walk-in conversion

TARGETED UPGRADES
Vanity, Tile & Fixture Work

Sometimes you don't need to start from scratch. New vanity, fresh tile, updated lighting, and better fixtures can completely change how a bathroom feels — at a fraction of the cost of a full remodel. We do a lot of these, and we take them just as seriously as the big projects.

Vanity replacement
Tile work

Mirror & storage

SATISFIED CLIENT, ROSEVILLE

OUR APPROACH
Bathroom Renovation Done
Without the Usual Headaches

The biggest complaints homeowners have about bathroom renovation contractors aren't about tile or fixtures. They're about contractors who don't communicate, timelines that stretch on, and costs that keep climbing after work starts.

Every project starts with a real walkthrough — not a quick glance and a ballpark figure. We measure, we ask the questions most people skip, and we look at what's actually behind the walls if we need to.

You get a line-by-line quote before we touch anything. If something unexpected comes up during the project, we tell you immediately — and we talk through options before acting.

1

We come see the space, measure everything, and ask the questions that matter before we talk about what it could look like.

We show up when we say we will and don't consider the job done until you do.
BATHROOM REMODELING SACRAMENTO
We Know Sacramento
Bathrooms

Bathroom remodeling in the Sacramento area comes up in nearly every renovation conversation we have — and usually because something has been quietly bothering the homeowner for longer than they'd like to admit. Cracked tile, a shower that never gets warm enough, a vanity from a different decade. Eventually it's just time.

A bathroom remodel in the Sacramento area can be as focused or as comprehensive as the situation calls for. We've done everything from full primary suite overhauls — new layout, custom tile, frameless glass, the works — to targeted fixes where we swap out the vanity, update the lighting, and replace the flooring. Both are legitimate projects and both deserve the same level of care.

If you've been searching for bathroom remodeling near me in the Sacramento area, we make the process simple from the first conversation to the final walkthrough. Real people answer the phone. Real estimates based on seeing your space.

CUSTOM CABINETRY SACRAMENTO CA

Storage That Fits Your Home, Not the Other Way Around

Most homes in the Sacramento area were built with cabinets chosen by a builder to meet a price point. They fit the space roughly. They hold things. They're not bad, exactly. They're just generic — and over time, generic starts to feel like settling.

Custom cabinetry is built to the exact dimensions of your space. Not close. Exact. That means no awkward gaps beside the refrigerator, no filler strips to hide where the cabinet didn't quite reach the wall, no wasted corner space. Every drawer, every shelf, every inch is planned before a single piece of wood is cut.

We're a custom cabinet builder in Sacramento CA. We design, build, and install cabinetry across all rooms — kitchens, bathrooms, living rooms, garages, home offices, and closets. Everything is made to order and installed by the same crew that built it. No outsourcing, no middlemen, no dropped balls between the shop and your home. Most of our clients come from referrals, and we've built cabinets in homes across Sacramento, Fair Oaks, Elk Grove, Folsom, Roseville, Granite Bay, and the surrounding communities.

If you're searching for custom cabinets near me in the Sacramento area, you're in the right place. We also work closely with our kitchen remodeling and bathroom remodeling teams — so if your project goes beyond cabinetry, we can handle the full scope under one roof.

Why homeowners choose custom over semi-custom or stock
✓
Built to the precise dimensions of your space, not a standard size that almost fits
✓
Material quality that stock and semi-custom cabinets simply can't match at any price point
✓
Joinery, drawer boxes, and hardware that hold up for decades, not years
✓
Design choices that are yours — wood species, stain, finish, profile, hardware
✓
Long-term value in your home that generic cabinetry doesn't deliver

CUSTOM CABINETRY SERVICES

Every Room, Built to Order

We build cabinetry for every room in the house. Each project is designed around the specific space, the way you use it, and the look you're going for. Here's what we typically build and install.

kitchen
Custom Kitchen Cabinets
This is where most of our projects start. We design complete kitchen cabinet layouts from scratch — upper and lower runs, islands, pantry towers, corner solutions that actually work. Every door profile, finish, and hardware choice is yours. We also build drawer box inserts, spice pullouts, trash cabinet assemblies, and anything else that makes a kitchen genuinely functional.
Full kitchen layouts
Island cabinetry
Pantry towers
Specialty inserts
bathtub
Custom Bathroom Cabinets
A vanity that's built to the actual width of your bathroom looks and feels completely different from one that was pulled off a shelf at a plumbing supply house. We build custom bathroom cabinets including single and double vanities, medicine cabinet built-ins, linen towers, and under-sink storage solutions. Any size, any finish, any configuration.
Custom vanities
Medicine cabinets
Linen storage
Tower cabinets
shelves
Built-In Cabinets for Living Rooms
Built-in cabinets for the living room are one of the most requested things we get calls about, and one of the projects that makes the biggest visual difference in a home. We build flanking bookcases, floor-to-ceiling storage walls, built-ins around fireplaces, and display shelving with concealed storage below. Every unit is designed to look like it was always part of the room.
Flanking bookcases
Fireplace built-ins
Storage walls
Display shelving
tv
Built-In Entertainment Centers
A well-built entertainment center hides all the cables and equipment that make a living room look messy while putting the TV and the things around it in exactly the right place. We design and build media wall units with concealed wiring runs, component ventilation, adjustable shelving, and integrated lighting. The result looks designed, not assembled.
Media walls
Cable management
Component storage
Integrated lighting
garage
Custom Garage Cabinets
Most garages in the Sacramento area have the same problem: everything is on the floor or hanging from a single wire shelf that bends under the weight. Proper garage storage cabinets change that completely. We design and build wall-mounted base cabinets, overhead storage units, and tall pantry-style lockers in durable finishes designed for garage conditions — sized to your actual walls, built from materials that hold up to heat and humidity, and installed so they don't come off the wall when you load them.

WHY CHOOSE CUSTOM CABINETS

Real Benefits, Honestly Stated

Custom cabinetry isn't for everyone and we'll tell you that upfront. But for homeowners who want something that lasts and actually fits, here's what you get.

01
Built to your exact space

Standard cabinets come in increments of 3 inches. Your kitchen probably doesn't. Custom cabinets fill the actual space you have, which means better layout, more storage, and no awkward filler pieces to hide the gaps. In a kitchen or bathroom especially, that difference is visible every single day.

02
Better materials, inside and out

The inside of a custom cabinet is just as well-built as the outside. Solid wood or high-grade plywood box construction, dovetail or dowel joinery on drawer boxes, full-extension soft-close slides. The things that determine how a cabinet holds up over ten or fifteen years are all handled properly because there's no budget pressure to cut them.

03
Are custom cabinets worth it?

For most homeowners who've priced out a quality semi-custom option and compared it side by side, the answer is yes. The material gap is significant. The fit is better. And unlike stock cabinets that need replacement in ten years, well-built custom cabinetry holds up for decades. The cost per year of use tends to be comparable once you do the math.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Questions We Hear Most Often

Straight answers, no marketing language.

Are custom cabinets really worth the extra cost?

It depends on your situation. If you're doing a quick flip and plan to sell in two years, semi-custom or stock cabinets might be the right call. But if you're staying in the home, the difference in material quality, longevity, and fit is substantial. Custom cabinets built with solid wood and proper joinery routinely last 25 to 40 years. Stock cabinets in the same kitchen often need replacement in 10 to 15. When you factor that in, the cost gap looks different.

We'll tell you honestly during the consultation if we think custom is or isn't the right fit for your project.

How long does it take to build and install custom cabinets?

Most projects run four to eight weeks from design approval to installation completion. The build itself is the majority of that time. Installation for a full kitchen typically takes three to five days. A single vanity or a living room built-in is usually done in one to two days on-site.

We lock in your production date when we take a deposit and update you throughout the build phase so you're not waiting in the dark.

Do you only do kitchens, or can you build cabinets for other rooms?

We build cabinetry for every room. Kitchens are common but we do a lot of bathroom vanities, living room built-ins, entertainment centers, home office systems, garage storage, and closets. In fact, some of our most satisfying projects are rooms outside the kitchen where a well-built built-in completely transforms how the space looks and functions.

Do you handle the design, or do I need to bring my own plans?

We handle the design. You don't need to come in with measurements, drawings, or anything beyond a general idea of what you're looking for. We take all the measurements on the walkthrough and develop the layout from there. We'll show you the design before anything is built and make changes until it's right.

If you do have inspiration photos or specific ideas, bring them. They're genuinely useful and help us understand what direction you're going faster than any questionnaire we could give you.

CUSTOM DECK BUILDER SACRAMENTO CA

A Deck That Fits Your Yard and How You Use It

Custom decks aren't just a platform attached to the back of a house. Done right, they extend your living space into the yard, create a spot people actually want to be in, and add real value to the property. Done wrong, they become a maintenance headache that looks dated in five years.

We're a deck contractor in Sacramento that designs and builds from scratch — no kit systems, no pre-designed templates. Every project starts with a site visit where we look at the grade of the yard, the orientation of the house, how the sun tracks across the space during the day, and what you're actually planning to do out there. That information shapes the design.

Most of our deck building in Sacramento happens in neighborhoods where backyards get real sun from March through October. Materials matter, shade matters, and the design has to work for how Sacramento summers actually feel. We factor all of that in before a single board goes down.

If your project also touches the inside of the house, we run the same crew across kitchen remodeling, bathroom remodeling, and custom cabinetry. One contractor, one schedule, one point of contact.

✓

✓
We do deck repairs on our own builds and on decks we didn't build

CUSTOM DECK BUILDING SERVICES

What We Design and Build

We handle every aspect of outdoor deck construction from design through installation — custom decks of all sizes, styles, and complexities. Here's a breakdown of what's typically included and what each service actually involves.

stairs
Multi-Level Deck Design
A multi-level deck is the right answer when the yard has grade changes, when you want to create distinct outdoor zones, or when a single platform would feel too large and visually flat. We design two-level deck configurations and more complex multi-tier layouts that transition naturally from the house to the yard. Steps, landings, and connections between levels are designed to feel like they belong together — not bolted on as an afterthought.

Built-In Seating and Storage
Freestanding furniture on a deck takes up floor space, blows around in the wind, and needs to be dragged inside every fall. Built-in deck seating is permanently attached to the structure, looks intentional, and can double as storage underneath. We build bench seating with flip-lid storage compartments, corner benches, and deck storage benches sized to whatever fits the layout.

We plan and install post cap lights, step lights, under-rail LED strips, and in-deck surface lighting. Everything runs through a proper outdoor-rated electrical circuit. We also rough in outlets and circuits for fans, speakers, or outdoor kitchen connections if the project calls for it.

WHY BUILD A CUSTOM DECK

Real Reasons to Invest in Outdoor Space

We're not going to tell you a deck will transform your life. But these are the things we hear homeowners say after the project is done.

01
You actually go outside

The number one thing homeowners tell us after a deck is finished is that they use their backyard more than they ever did before. A ground-level yard without a defined space tends to be somewhere you walk through. A deck with seating, lighting, and a comfortable surface is somewhere you stay. Sacramento's climate makes this worthwhile nine months of the year.

02
It adds real value

A quality outdoor deck consistently shows up in appraisals and buyer interest when homeowners eventually sell. The return varies by design and material, but a well-built deck made from durable materials in a climate where outdoor living is valued isn't a discretionary feature — it's expected. It adds square footage to the functional living area of the home.

03
Quality matters more than you'd think

A cheap deck built on undersized posts with inadequate footings will move, creak, and degrade faster than the wood you're standing on. Proper deck installation means correct footing depth for the soil conditions, properly spaced structural members, and materials that match the climate. We do this right because cutting corners on a deck shows up fast and is expensive to fix.

DECKING MATERIALS

How the Main Materials Actually Compare

A straightforward look at what we install most often in Sacramento and what each material is really like to live with — without the brand pitch. For the full breakdown, see our guide on composite vs. hardwood decking in Northern California.

	Composite / Trex	Wood (Redwood, Cedar, Ipe)
Annual maintenance	No staining or sealing required	Cleaning and sealing every 1–2 years
Heat in direct summer sun	Can run warm — lighter colors recommended	Stays cooler underfoot
Lifespan	25 to 30 years (premium lines longer)	15 to 25 years for redwood/cedar; 40+ for ipe
Splintering and cracking	None	Common over time, especially in dry climates
Look and feel	Consistent, modern, slightly engineered	Natural grain, warmer character
Upfront cost	Mid to high — premium composite is comparable to hardwood	Low to very high (pressure-treated to ipe)
Best fit	Homeowners who want low maintenance and long life	Homeowners who want a natural look and accept the upkeep

DECK COST SACRAMENTO

How Much Does a Deck Cost?

This is genuinely one of the hardest questions to answer without seeing the site. Deck cost in Sacramento depends on more variables than most outdoor projects — the size and layout, the material choice, the height off the ground, whether footings need to go deep because of soil conditions, and whether electrical or shade structures are part of the scope.

What we can tell you is that a simple ground-level deck in pressure-treated wood is a significantly different investment than a multi-level composite deck with built-in seating, lighting, and a pergola. Both are legitimate projects. The right one depends on what you're trying to accomplish and what you want to spend.

We give you a written, line-by-line quote after the site visit. Every material, every labor category, every permit fee is listed separately so you can see exactly where the cost comes from and make informed decisions about where to spend and where to simplify.

straighten
Deck size and layout
Square footage is the biggest driver. Multi-level designs add structural complexity and cost. Irregular shapes also take more material and labor than simple rectangles.
layers
Material selection
Pressure-treated wood is the most affordable surface. Composite lines like Trex are mid-range. Hardwood in ipe or tigerwood costs significantly more but can last twice as long.
foundation
Deck height and footing depth
Taller decks require more structural framing and longer posts. Sacramento's clay-heavy soils sometimes require deeper footings than other regions, which affects both cost and timeline.
add_circle
Added features
Built-in seating, deck lighting, a pergola, cable railing — each of these adds to the scope and the cost. We price them as individual line items so you can add or remove them based on your budget.
The only way to get a real number is to see the yard.
We come out, take measurements, talk through the design, and put together a written quote — at no cost to you. No obligation, no pressure.

OUR DECK CONSTRUCTION PROCESS

How a Deck Project Actually Gets Built

Four stages, clearly communicated. Here's what happens from your first call to the day you're sitting on the finished deck.

01
Site visit and assessment
We come to your home, walk the yard, assess the grade and soil conditions, note the sun orientation, and ask about how you plan to use the space. Takes about an hour and costs nothing.
→
02
Design and material selection
We develop a layout, walk you through material options with honest guidance on cost and performance, and put together a written, itemized quote. You review, ask questions, and make changes before anything is agreed to.
→
03
Permits and construction
Most decks in Sacramento require a building permit — we handle the application and inspections on every project. Then we build from the ground up: footings, framing, decking surface, railings, lighting, and any added features.
→

We've built custom decks in neighborhoods across Sacramento from East Sac and Land Park to Natomas and Elk Grove. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Questions We Hear Most Often

Honest answers from people who've been building decks in Sacramento for years.

Do I need a permit to build a deck in Sacramento?

In most cases, yes. Any deck attached to a house in Sacramento requires a building permit. Freestanding decks over a certain height or square footage typically require permits as well. The exact rules depend on whether you're in the city of Sacramento, the county, or an incorporated area like Folsom or Roseville.

We pull permits on every project. Some homeowners ask us to skip it to save time and money. We don't. Unpermitted decks create problems when you sell and can create liability issues if something happens on the structure.

How long does a custom deck build take?

A straightforward single-level deck on a flat lot can be completed in one to two weeks once permits are approved. A multi-level deck with built-in features, lighting, and a pergola might run three to four weeks on-site.

The part that takes longest usually isn't construction — it's permit approval. Sacramento-area building departments vary in turnaround from two to six weeks depending on jurisdiction and time of year. We account for this in the timeline and order materials during the permit window so there's no delay once approval comes through.

Is composite decking really worth it over wood?

For most Sacramento homeowners, yes. Composite decking costs more upfront but doesn't require the annual or biennial maintenance that wood does. In Sacramento's climate — hot, dry summers followed by wet winters — wood decks that aren't maintained regularly deteriorate faster than people expect.

That said, a properly maintained wood deck has a warmth and character composite hasn't fully replicated. We'll walk you through both and help you decide based on what matters to you.

Do you also handle deck repairs and maintenance?

Yes. We work as deck repair contractors on existing structures regardless of who originally built them. The most common Sacramento-area issues we see are corroded post bases, ledger boards that weren't properly flashed and have let water in, decking surface boards that have cracked or cupped, and railings with loose posts.

We'll come out and assess the structure honestly. Sometimes a repair makes more sense than a rebuild. Sometimes it doesn't, and we'll tell you that upfront.

SIDING INSTALLATION SACRAMENTO CA

Exterior Cladding That Holds Up to Sacramento

Siding is the part of your house that takes the most direct hit from weather, sun, and time. Sacramento's combination of heat, UV, occasional storms, and seasonal humidity is harder on exterior cladding than people realize. Done well, siding protects the structure underneath for decades. Done poorly, it traps moisture, rots out from behind, and fails years before it should.

We install fiber cement, board and batten, T1-11, vinyl, and stucco across the greater Sacramento region. Every project starts with a real look at what's there — substrate, flashing, existing moisture issues — before we quote anything. Every install includes proper house wrap and moisture barrier as a standard step, not an upcharge.

If you're looking for a siding contractor near you in Sacramento, Fair Oaks, Folsom, Roseville, Granite Bay, El Dorado Hills, or anywhere in between, we're happy to come take a look. We also coordinate with our kitchen, bathroom, and custom cabinetry teams when siding is part of a larger remodel — one company, one schedule, one point of contact.

What we always include — even when it's not asked for
✓
Substrate inspection before any new siding goes up
✓
Code-compliant house wrap and moisture barrier installation
✓
Flashing at every penetration — pipes, wires, light fixtures
✓
Manufacturer-spec fasteners and nail schedules (Hardie, etc.)
✓
Caulking from the approved product list — not whatever's on the truck
✓
Daily site cleanup — old siding and packaging leave when we leave

STYLE POSSIBILITIES

What Fiber Cement Actually Looks Like

James Hardie products give you a wide range of looks — modern, transitional, craftsman, farmhouse, classic. Here's a quick visual reference for what's possible when you mix profiles, colors, and trim details. Every photo below shows real James Hardie material — the same products we install on Sacramento homes.

Craftsman with shingle accents
Hardie Shingle gables paired with timber porch detail — a classic Sacramento look.
Hardie Plank in navy
Crisp lap profile with white trim and soffit — fiber cement's most common installation.
Modern farmhouse, all white

Cape Cod shingle detail

Vertical Hardie Panel with batten strips — strong street presence with white column trim.
Architectural panel, modern lines
Smooth Hardie Architectural Panel for clean, contemporary geometry.
Moody, modern, dark exterior
Hardie Plank in deep charcoal — pre-finished color holds up against UV without repainting.

Every James Hardie color shown above is available in ColorPlus® factory finish, with a 15-year color warranty. Photos courtesy of James Hardie Building Products.

WHAT WE DO

Siding Services, Honestly Stated

Whether you need a small repair, a full replacement, or new siding on a room addition, here's the work we actually do — and how we approach it.

deployed_code
Full Siding Installation
New siding from scratch — substrate inspection, house wrap, siding installation, trim, and caulking. We do this on new construction, room additions, garages, and full exterior replacements.
change_circle
Siding Replacement
When siding has reached the end of its life — or was installed poorly the first time — we remove everything down to the sheathing, address what we find, and start fresh. No patching over problems.
construction
Siding Repair
Rotted boards, impact damage, failed caulk, cracked corners. We repair what needs repairing and leave the rest. If a repair doesn't make sense, we'll say so and explain why.
shield
Waterproofing & House Wrap
Siding is only as good as what's behind it. Every installation includes proper house wrap and moisture barrier. We don't skip this step — even when nobody asks about it.
grid_on
Stucco Repair & Re-Stucco
We do stucco work too — patching cracked or damaged sections, re-stuccoing walls that have failed, and installing new stucco systems with proper lath, paper, and flashing details on additions and remodels.
straighten
Trim & Finish Work
Corner boards, window trim, door casings, and fascia — these are the details that separate a finished job from one that just looks done. We include them and we take our time on them.
find_in_page
Pre-Installation Rot Inspection
Before any new siding goes on, we check the substrate behind the existing material. Hidden rot is common in Sacramento homes — we find it and deal with it before it gets covered up again.
format_paint
Color-Match & Custom Trim
When we repair existing siding, we source matching profiles and finishes wherever possible so repairs aren't obvious. Custom trim, gable boards, banding, and belly bands get careful layout.
inventory_2
Board Replacement
Localized siding board replacement for damaged sections — usually near a window, at the base of a wall, or at a corner where caulk failed. We address the moisture source first, then close it back up.
Not sure which scope fits your house?
We come out, look at what you have, and tell you straight whether you're looking at a repair, a replacement, or somewhere in between. Free consultation, no pressure.
GET A FREE ESTIMATE →

TYPES OF SIDING WE INSTALL

Materials We Work With Every Day

The right siding material depends on the house, the budget, and what the homeowner is willing to maintain. We install several types and we're honest about the pros and cons of each. Here's what we use most often in the Sacramento area and why — or read our full comparison of siding options for Sacramento's climate.

Fiber Cement Siding

This is the material we install most frequently, and if someone asks us what holds up best in Sacramento's climate, fiber cement is usually the answer. It doesn't rot, it doesn't burn, it resists insects, and it holds paint significantly longer than wood. Fiber cement siding installation takes more skill than vinyl — the material is heavy, requires specific fasteners, and needs to be handled carefully to avoid cracking — but the results are worth it.

We're a certified installer of James Hardie siding, the most recognized brand in fiber cement. Hardie board siding comes in lap, vertical board, and shingle profiles, and it's available in a ColorPlus factory finish that carries a much longer paint warranty than field-painted material.

For homes with existing fiber cement that has cracked or developed surface issues, we also do fiber cement siding repair — matching the profile and finish as closely as possible so repairs aren't obvious.

30+ year lifespan
Fire resistant
James Hardie certified
Paintable or pre-finished
Low maintenance
Fiber cement lap profile
The most common installation in Sacramento-area homes. Durable, low-maintenance, and takes paint well.
Board and Batten Siding

Board and batten siding has become one of the most requested exterior styles over the past several years. The vertical lines make a house look taller and more substantial. It reads as both traditional and contemporary depending on the colors and trim details. A lot of homes being built or remodeled in Sacramento right now use it as either a full exterior treatment or as an accent on specific walls.

Board and batten exterior siding can be done in fiber cement, wood, or engineered wood. Each has different maintenance and cost profiles — we'll walk you through what makes sense for your house. The installation approach varies depending on whether you're going over existing siding or starting from sheathing.

Vertical profile
Fiber cement or wood
High visual impact
Full or accent walls
Board and batten profile
Vertical board with narrow batten strips covering the seams. Strong visual presence from the street.
T1-11 Siding

T1-11 siding is a sheet-style product, typically sold in T1-11 4x8 panels with vertical grooves cut into the face to give it a board-and-batten appearance. It's most common on garages, workshops, sheds, and older accessory structures. It installs quickly and is relatively inexpensive.

The main thing to understand about T1-11 is that it's more maintenance-sensitive than fiber cement or vinyl. If it's not kept sealed and painted, it takes on moisture and can degrade faster than expected. We install it on garages and outbuildings where it makes sense — and we always make sure the bottom edge is cut properly, the seams are addressed, and the whole thing is primed before paint goes on.

Sheet panel format
Common on garages and sheds
Quick installation
Requires regular sealing
T1-11 panel profile
Full-sheet panel with routed grooves. Common on garages, workshops, and older outbuildings.
Vinyl Siding

Vinyl isn't the most exciting material to talk about, but there are real situations where it's the right call. It's the most affordable option, it never needs painting, and it doesn't rot or rust. For rental properties, budget-conscious projects, or situations where low maintenance is the absolute priority, vinyl siding makes sense.

Bad vinyl siding installation shows immediately — improper overlap, visible nail heads, buckling from over-nailing, gaps at j-channel. We don't install vinyl house siding the way some crews do, fast and loose with the details. It deserves the same attention as any other material: nail it loose so it can move, give panels room at openings, miter-lock the j-channel at corners, and take time on the details most crews rush through.

Most affordable option
No painting required
Wide color selection
Lightweight installation
Vinyl lap profile
Lightweight, affordable, and maintenance-free. Best for rentals or budget-driven projects.
Stucco Cladding

A lot of Sacramento and surrounding-area homes are clad in stucco — particularly newer subdivision builds and Mediterranean-style homes. We do stucco repair and re-stucco work, plus new three-coat stucco installation on additions, garages, and full exterior projects.

Most stucco work we get called out for is stucco crack repair and patching of damaged sections. Hairline cracks are normal and cosmetic. Wider cracks, bulging, or staining usually indicate moisture intrusion behind the finish — and that's where it matters that we open it up properly, check the lath and paper underneath, and address the source before we close it back up. New stucco installs get proper weep screed at the bottom, two layers of grade-D building paper, galvanized lath fastened to spec, and a scratch–brown–finish coat schedule that gives the system time to cure between layers.

Three-coat system
Crack & patch repair

Color & texture matched

WHAT WE ACTUALLY DO ON SITE

The Work, Explained Plainly

Here's what different scopes of siding work actually look like from our end. Not marketing language — just what happens.

01
Full Board and Batten Installations

A full board and batten siding installation means we're working from the sheathing outward. House wrap goes on first, then furring or blocking at regular intervals to create a flat nailing surface, then the boards, then the battens. We pay close attention to the base detail at the bottom of the wall and the top termination at the eaves — these are where most installations fail to look intentional.

COMMON INSTALLATION MISTAKE

A lot of board and batten jobs we've repaired had battens nailed directly through the boards into the sheathing. This restricts wood movement and leads to cracking. Proper installation leaves the boards free to expand and fastens the battens on each side of the seam, not through the face.

02
Fiber Cement Work

As a James Hardie siding contractor, we follow the manufacturer's installation requirements on every job. That means specific nail schedules, minimum clearances from grade and roofing, proper joint flashing, and caulk from the approved product list. Fiber cement siding installation done outside those specs voids the warranty — something homeowners often don't find out until they need to make a claim.

On repair work, we cut sections cleanly with the right blade, match the existing profile, and prime all cut edges before installation. If we're matching an existing painted finish, we do our best — and we're honest when a perfect match isn't possible.

03
Stucco Repair & Re-Stucco

For stucco crack repair, we route the crack out, clean it, and patch it with a properly mixed material that matches the surrounding texture as closely as possible. For larger sections, we cut back to sound material, replace any compromised lath or paper, and rebuild the system in proper coats. New stucco gets a real three-coat application — scratch, brown, and finish — with cure time between each layer instead of a one-coat shortcut that cracks within a year.

04
Custom Trim Work

Exterior trim installation is where the quality of a siding job is really visible. Corner boards need to be plumb and tight. Window trim needs to be caulked at the right points and back-primed before it goes up. Fascia needs to be properly flashed at the top edge so water doesn't run behind it. Custom trim siding work — decorative gable boards, banding, belly bands — requires careful layout and real attention to how it reads from the street.

05
Waterproofing & Protection

Every siding job we do includes house wrap installation as a standard step, not an add-on. A quality siding moisture barrier is what actually keeps water out of the wall cavity when siding is compromised, at penetrations like windows and outlets, and during the inevitable years before paint is refreshed. We use code-compliant materials and lap everything in the right direction — top overlapping bottom, just like shingles.

We also pay specific attention to penetrations — anywhere a pipe, wire, or light fixture goes through the siding is a potential leak point. These get properly flashed and sealed before the siding goes on around them.

06
Repair Work Across All Materials

Siding rot repair is probably half of what we get called out for. Usually it's localized — a section near a window, at the base of a wall where water has been pooling, or at a corner where caulk failed years ago. We don't just replace the visible board. We probe the surrounding area, check what's behind the damaged section, and address the source of the moisture before siding board replacement closes everything back up.

We do repairs on all the materials we install — fiber cement, wood, vinyl, T1-11, and stucco. The goal is always for the repair to be as invisible as possible, which usually means sourcing matching material rather than using whatever's on the truck.

WHY HOMEOWNERS CHOOSE US

What We're Actually Like to Work With

Most of the work we get comes from referrals. A neighbor sees a job we finished and asks who did it. A homeowner uses us once, moves to a new house, and calls us again. That's not an accident — it's what happens when a crew shows up, communicates clearly, and does what they said they were going to do.

We're not the cheapest siding installation option in the Sacramento area and we don't try to be. We're the crew that shows up on time, keeps you updated, doesn't leave a mess at the end of the day, and actually cares about how the finished job looks. That matters more than it sounds.

We also try to be honest when something is outside what we'd recommend. If the substrate behind your old siding is so compromised that a repair isn't the right call, we'll tell you. If you're asking us to install a material we don't think will hold up well in your specific situation, we'll say so and explain why. You can still make whatever decision you want — it's your house. But you'll make it with accurate information.

"These guys came out, looked at what we had, and told us straight that the back of the house had more rot behind the siding than we'd budgeted for. They could have just replaced what was visible and moved on. Instead they showed us what they found and we figured out the right fix together. Whole job took a week. Everything looks great."
— Past client, Fair Oaks, CA · Full board and batten installation
schedule
We show up when we say we will
Seems obvious, but it's the thing homeowners mention most. We give you a start date and we're there. If something changes, we call you — not the other way around.
description
Written, itemized quotes
You get a real quote with materials and labor broken out. Not a number on a napkin. You can see exactly what you're paying for before you decide.
location_on
