FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Questions We Get All the Time

Real answers, not boilerplate.

What types of siding are best for houses in Sacramento?

When homeowners ask about the types of siding for houses in this area, we almost always come back to fiber cement as the strongest overall choice. It handles Sacramento's heat and UV exposure well, resists the fire risk that's real in this region, doesn't rot, and holds paint longer than wood. James Hardie is the most common brand we install and it has a solid track record.

Board and batten in fiber cement is increasingly common and looks great on a lot of homes. Stucco is the dominant exterior on newer subdivisions and works well when installed and maintained properly. Vinyl is a reasonable choice for rental properties and tight budgets. T1-11 makes sense on garages and outbuildings where cost and speed are the priorities, as long as you're prepared to keep up with painting and sealing.

The honest answer is that the best siding for your house depends on your budget, your maintenance tolerance, and the style of the home. We'll give you our recommendation based on all three when we come out.

How much does siding installation cost in Sacramento?

The siding installation cost depends on the material, the square footage, the condition of what's behind the existing siding, and how much trim and detail work is involved. Vinyl is the most affordable. Fiber cement runs higher but lasts considerably longer. Stucco and specialty materials cost more still.

What we can tell you is that we give you a written, itemized quote before we start. Material costs and labor are listed separately, so you can see exactly where the money goes. If the substrate turns out to be in worse shape than expected once we open things up, we'll tell you before we proceed, not after.

Do you do stucco repair as well as siding?

Yes. We handle stucco repair, re-stucco work, and new three-coat stucco installation alongside the rest of our siding services. A lot of Sacramento homes — especially newer subdivisions and Mediterranean-style builds — are clad in stucco, and we get called out regularly for crack repair, patching of damaged sections, and full re-stucco where the existing finish has failed.

For new stucco we install proper weep screed, two layers of grade-D paper, galvanized lath, and a real scratch–brown–finish coat schedule with cure time between layers.

Can I install T1-11 siding myself?

People ask us about how to install T1-11 siding and whether it's something they could take on themselves. The material itself isn't complicated — it's large panels and the fastening schedule is straightforward. But the things that cause problems are the details: proper sealing of all edges including cuts, correct bottom clearance from grade, getting the panels truly plumb, and making sure every seam is addressed so water can't track behind.

On a small shed or workshop, a careful DIYer can do it. On a house — or any structure where you care about the result lasting — we'd recommend having it done professionally.

How is vinyl siding installed?

The basics of vinyl siding installation are: a starter strip at the bottom, each course locking into the one below, and j-channel around windows and at corners to terminate the panels cleanly.

The part that separates a quality job from a poor one is the fastening and fitting. Vinyl expands and contracts significantly with temperature changes. If it's nailed too tight, it buckles. If panels aren't cut to allow for movement at openings, you get gaps. And if the j-channel isn't cut and miter-locked properly at corners, it looks amateur. We nail it loose, give it room to move, and take time on the details that most crews rush.

WINDOW REPLACEMENT IN THE SACRAMENTO AREA
New Windows,
Done Without the Drama.

Replacing the windows in your house should feel like a meaningful upgrade — not a high-pressure sales pitch followed by months of headaches. We install replacement windows in Sacramento and surrounding communities, and we've kept the process intentionally simple.

You tell us what's bothering you about your current windows — drafts, condensation between the panes, stuck sashes, sky-high summer cooling bills, old aluminum frames that rattle in the wind — and we tell you honestly what your options are. We don't push one brand for everything. Anlin, Milgard, and Andersen each have a sweet spot, and we match the brand and the install method to what your house actually needs.

The Sacramento climate is hard on old windows. Single-pane glass and early dual-pane units from the 1980s and 1990s are no match for a July afternoon on the Central Valley floor. Heat bleeds in, cool air bleeds out, and your utility bills tell the story. Modern energy efficient windows change that in a measurable way. We've seen homeowners report meaningful drops in cooling costs after a full-house replacement, and the comfort difference is immediate.

Same crew from the first measure to the final caulk bead. No subcontractors who've never been to your house before. We also handle kitchen remodeling, bathroom remodeling, and siding work if your project goes beyond the windows.

WINDOW STYLES WE INSTALL
Every Style, Every Opening.

From standard bedroom windows to large picture windows facing a backyard view, we install every common style — and the less common ones too. Here's what each one actually is and when it makes sense.

MOST COMMON
Single-Hung Windows

The lower sash slides up, the upper sash stays fixed. Single-hung windows are the standard in most Sacramento homes built before 2000. They're affordable, easy to operate, and work well in bedrooms and bathrooms where you want ventilation without the mechanical complexity of a casement. If your house already has them, retrofit replacement is usually clean and straightforward.

MORE VENTILATION CONTROL
Double-Hung Windows

Both sashes move — up and down — which gives you more control over airflow and makes the windows easier to clean from inside. Double-hung vs single-hung is often a matter of preference and budget. Double-hungs cost a bit more but many homeowners find them worth it for the cleaning convenience alone, especially on upper floors. Available through all three brands we carry.

GREAT FOR WIDER OPENINGS
Sliding Windows

Panels slide horizontally rather than up and down. Sliding windows work particularly well in wider openings over kitchen sinks, in family rooms, or anywhere a taller single-hung wouldn't fit cleanly. They have fewer moving parts than a casement, which means less to go wrong over time. The XO and OX configurations let you choose which panel slides.

IDEAL ABOVE COUNTERS
Awning Windows

Awning windows are hinged at the top and swing outward from the bottom. Because they seal tightly when closed and can be opened partway during light rain, they're popular in bathrooms, above kitchen counters, and in utility spaces. They don't work in every opening — you need clearance outside — but where they do fit, they're practical and draft-resistant.

SAFETY AND CODE COMPLIANCE
Egress Windows

An egress window is a minimum-size openable window required by code in sleeping rooms and finished basements. Basement egress windows often require well excavation and structural work around the opening, but the code requirement is real — especially if you're finishing a basement or converting a garage space. We assess the existing opening and recommend the right window and method.

MAXIMUM LIGHT
Picture and Fixed Windows

Fixed windows don't open — they're all glass, maximum light, unobstructed views. They pair naturally with operable windows on either side when you want the light from a large opening but also need some ventilation. Picture windows in living rooms and dining areas are some of our favorite installations because the visual impact is significant and the install itself is clean.

CLASSIC OPERATION
Casement Windows

Hinged on the side and swung open with a hand crank, casement windows seal very tightly when closed — better than most other styles. They're ideal for rooms where security and energy performance are priorities, and they're what we recommend for high-wind exposures. The crank mechanism requires occasional maintenance but the seal quality is hard to beat.

PREMIUM INSTALLATIONS
Bay and Bow Windows

Bay windows project out from the wall and typically combine three window units — a center picture window flanked by two casements or single-hungs at an angle. They add floor space, light, and visual interest from both inside and outside. Bow windows are similar but use four or more units in a curved arrangement. Both require structural consideration at the header. We handle the full scope.

Not sure which style fits your opening?

We come out, look at the openings, and recommend the right window for each one. No obligation, no pressure — just a straight answer.

SCHEDULE A FREE MEASURE
ENERGY PERFORMANCE
Built for Sacramento
Summers and Winters.

The technology inside a modern replacement window is what actually makes the difference on your utility bill. Here's what's doing the work.

01
Low-E Coatings

Low-emissivity glass has a microscopically thin metallic coating that reflects infrared radiation — specifically summer heat — back outside before it gets into your home. In Sacramento's climate, this is probably the single most impactful technology in a replacement window. It works in winter too, keeping interior heat from escaping through the glass.

02
Argon Gas Fill

The space between panes in a dual-pane or triple pane window is filled with argon gas rather than air. Argon is denser and transfers heat more slowly, which improves the overall thermal performance of the glass unit. Most windows from Anlin, Milgard, and Andersen include argon fill as standard in their better product lines. It's not something you see, but you feel the result.

03
Triple Pane Glass

Triple pane windows add a third layer of glass and a second gas-filled cavity, which dramatically reduces heat transfer compared to dual-pane. They're more common in colder climates, but for Sacramento homeowners who want maximum performance in a home office that faces west or a bedroom that gets direct afternoon sun, triple pane is worth the extra investment.

04
Noise Insulation

A good modern window is quieter than what you probably have now. Noise insulation windows — specifically dual and triple pane units with laminated glass options — significantly reduce outdoor sound transmission. If you're on a busy street or near a school, the acoustic improvement from replacing single-pane windows can be as valuable as the energy savings. Anlin and Milgard both offer laminated glass packages for this purpose.

05
Frame Efficiency

The frame conducts heat just like the glass does. Vinyl frames have natural insulating properties and don't conduct heat the way aluminum does. Fiberglass frames perform even better — they're dimensionally stable, don't expand and contract significantly with temperature changes, and create a tighter, more consistent seal over decades of use. The frame you choose affects long-term performance, not just the day the windows go in.

06
Energy Star Ratings

Every window we install from Anlin and Milgard meets Energy Star requirements for the Northern California climate zone. Andersen products at the 400 Series level and above also qualify. This matters practically because it may qualify you for utility rebates — check with your local utility before we start, and we'll make sure the products we spec qualify.

FRAME MATERIALS
Vinyl, Wood,
Fiberglass, Aluminum.

Frame material affects everything — cost, energy performance, lifespan, and how the window looks from inside and out. Vinyl replacement windows are the most popular choice in Sacramento for good reason, but they're not right for every home or every homeowner. Here's a plain-language rundown.

Custom windows from Andersen in particular give you significant flexibility on frame profile, interior finish, and hardware — useful when you're matching an existing architectural style or specifying something for a room where the window is meant to be noticed.

ASK ABOUT FRAME OPTIONS
Vinyl
Most popular in Sacramento. Energy efficient, maintenance-free, available in a range of colors. Anlin and Milgard both have strong vinyl lines. The right choice for most replacement projects.
Fiberglass
More dimensionally stable than vinyl — it expands and contracts less with temperature swings. Stronger sightlines, better long-term seal integrity. Milgard Essence and Andersen are the main options we install.
Wood-Clad
Wood interior, aluminum or fiberglass exterior. The best of both worlds for homes where interior wood trim matters — craftsmans, ranches, older East Sacramento homes. Andersen 400 Series is the standard here.
Aluminum
Best for very large openings and homes with a modern or industrial aesthetic. Not the strongest thermal performer, but Milgard's aluminum line includes thermal breaks to help. Available for commercial-style openings where vinyl and fiberglass don't go.
HOW WE INSTALL
Four Install Methods,
One That's Right for Your House.

Most window companies know one method and apply it everywhere. We use four — and we'll tell you which one your home actually needs after we see the wall condition, existing frame, and exterior finish. The method matters as much as the window itself.

MOST THOROUGH
Full Frame Window Replacement

We remove the entire window assembly down to the studs — frame, sill, everything — and install a new flanged window with proper flashing, house wrap integration, and interior and exterior trim. This is the right method when there's dry rot, water damage, or a failing frame. It's more disruptive and more expensive than a retrofit, but the long-term result is better and the warranty stays fully intact.

Full frame replacement is also required when you're changing the rough opening size — making a window larger or adding a new opening where there wasn't one. We assess structural implications and pull permits when required.

Full demolition
New flashing
Trim included
Permit required
MOST COMMON
Retrofit Window Installation

The new window installs inside the existing frame, which stays in place. No exterior demolition, no interior trim damage, no stucco or siding repair. Retrofit window installation is the fastest, cleanest, and most affordable method — and it's appropriate for most Sacramento-area homes where the existing frame is structurally sound.

The trade-off is that the new window's glass area is slightly smaller than the opening, since the new frame sits inside the old one. For most windows this is imperceptible. For very large picture windows it can be more noticeable, and full-frame may be worth considering.

Existing frame stays
Fast and clean
No exterior damage
No paint touch-up
STUCCO HOMES
Over-Stucco Install

A retrofit variant for stucco homes. We use a Z-bar or block-frame window that seals against your existing stucco without cracking it open. This saves the cost and mess of stucco patching while still delivering a watertight, properly sealed install. Common in Roseville, Elk Grove, and Folsom subdivisions built from the 1990s through 2010s.

No stucco demolition
Z-bar or block frame
Watertight seal
SIDING HOMES
Over-Siding Install

A flush-fin retrofit window tucks neatly under your existing siding course. No siding patching, no exterior work. Ideal for ranch homes, craftsmans, and any home with existing fiber cement, wood, or vinyl siding. We work closely with our siding team when a window replacement and exterior re-siding are happening at the same time — one crew, one schedule, one point of contact.

Flush-fin profile
No siding removal
Ranch and craftsman-friendly
ON WINDOW REPLACEMENT COST

The window replacement cost for a full-house project in Sacramento varies considerably based on the install method, the brand, and the number and size of windows. Retrofit in a mid-tier Milgard or Anlin product is significantly different from full-frame Andersen with custom interior trim. We give you a written, line-by-line quote after the measure — not a range that means nothing. If budget is a constraint, we'll tell you where you can spend less without compromising the result.

SLIDING PATIO DOORS
Sliding Doors
From the Same Brands.

A sliding patio door that sticks, drafts, or rattles is one of those things that bothers you every single day. And yet it's easy to put off. Modern sliding glass door replacement from Anlin, Milgard, or Andersen is one of the most satisfying upgrades in a remodel — the difference in how the door operates, seals, and looks is immediate.

We install two-panel sliders, three-panel XOX configurations, and larger multi slide door systems for living rooms and dining areas that open onto a patio or deck. For homeowners who want the opening to disappear entirely, pocket doors that slide into the wall cavity are an option we handle as part of a broader remodel scope.

The same install methods apply — retrofit slider replacement when the existing frame is sound, full-frame when it's not. We'll assess and tell you which approach makes sense.

WHY REPLACE THE SLIDER NOW?

An old slider adds to your cooling load the same way windows do — sometimes more, because the glass area is larger. A new sealed unit from Anlin or Milgard with low-E glass and argon fill makes a measurable difference. If your patio door is more than 15 years old and you're already doing windows, doing both at the same time saves on labor and keeps the project clean.

Sacramento Climate.

Sacramento summers are brutal on old windows. Single-pane and early dual-pane units bleed heat in both directions — the AC runs constantly in July, and rooms feel cold in January despite the heater running. Modern replacement windows in Sacramento CA from Anlin, Milgard, and Andersen are engineered specifically for climates like ours.

We've installed windows in homes from midtown craftsmans to El Dorado Hills new builds. We know which install method works on which kind of wall, what permits Sacramento County and the surrounding cities require, and how to keep the manufacturer warranty intact through every step. That experience saves you money and prevents the second-trip callbacks that happen when installers cut corners.

HOME REMODELING SACRAMENTO CA

Sacramento Homes That Finally Match What You Paid For Them

Remodeling in Sacramento means working across very different generations of housing. A Land Park or Curtis Park bungalow may call for careful investigation of older wiring, drain lines, or wall construction, while a mid-century ranch or newer Natomas home presents a different set of layout and finish decisions. We start by learning what is actually in your house.

For home remodeling in Sacramento, the existing conditions shape the scope. We inspect the space, discuss how you want it to function, and identify where opening walls, moving utilities, or changing structure may add design or permit work. Projects that require permits go through the City of Sacramento's Building Division rather than a suburban or county process.

Our role is to turn that assessment into a clear plan: what can stay, what should change, which decisions need to happen before demolition, and what each part of the work costs. You receive a written, itemized quote before construction begins and a call before any approved scope changes.

Why Sacramento homeowners keep recommending us
✓
Older-house questions are investigated before new finishes conceal them
✓
City permit requirements are included in planning when the scope calls for them

✓

OUR SERVICES

Full Home Remodeling, All from One Crew

We stay focused on what we do well. Kitchens, bathrooms, additions, and full renovations. Every project gets the same attention whether it's one room or the whole house.

— 01
Kitchen Remodeling
Cabinet replacement, stone countertops, layout redesigns, new flooring, and lighting. We work around how your household actually uses the kitchen, not a floor plan from a catalog.
— 02
Bathroom Remodeling
Shower remodels, tub conversions, custom tile, vanity upgrades, and flooring. Guest bath refresh or full primary suite overhaul. Same quality of work either way.
— 03
Home Additions
Extra bedrooms, expanded living areas, ADUs, home offices. Permits, design coordination, and the full build from one point of contact.
— 04
Full Home Renovation
Multiple rooms, all trades coordinated. We map the sequence so each phase completes in the right order and nothing has to be redone.
— 05
Targeted Upgrades
One room, one system, one thing that needs fixing. Sometimes a focused scope is exactly the right call. We'll tell you honestly if that's the case.
— 06
Custom Work
Built-ins, specialty tile, custom cabinetry, and projects where the details really matter. If you have something specific in mind, tell us and we'll tell you what it actually takes.

KITCHEN REMODELING SACRAMENTO

Kitchens That Actually Catch Up to the House Around Them

A kitchen remodel in Sacramento usually starts with the same list of complaints. The cabinets are that golden oak color that dates the whole room the moment you walk in. The tile countertop has a grout problem that's never going away no matter how many times it gets sealed. The lighting is a single can overhead and a fluorescent strip under the upper cabinets that flickers. The layout is fine but nothing about it feels intentional.

Kitchen remodeling in Sacramento CA at its most common scope means new semi-custom cabinetry in a painted finish, quartz countertops, a proper tile or stone backsplash, and layered lighting that actually makes the room usable. Most of these projects run four to five weeks from demo to final punch list. The layout usually stays because moving the sink or the range means touching plumbing or gas, and most homeowners would rather put that budget into materials and finishes.

WHAT WE FIND IN SACRAMENTO KITCHENS FROM THE EARLY 2000S

In an older Sacramento kitchen, a finish-only plan can change after the existing cabinets come out. Walls and floors may be out of level, utility locations may not suit the new layout, and older electrical or plumbing may need evaluation. We document those conditions, explain the options, and obtain approval before work outside the quoted scope proceeds.

When a homeowner wants to change the actual layout — open the kitchen to the dining room, add an island, relocate the sink — we handle the full scope. Structural assessment, permits, utility coordination. Kitchen remodel in Sacramento CA at that level typically runs six to eight weeks. The result is a fundamentally different room, not just an updated one.

BATHROOM REMODELING SACRAMENTO

Bathrooms That Feel Like Someone Actually Designed Them

Most Sacramento homes came with two and a half or three bathrooms. The primary has a double vanity, a soaking tub that nobody uses, and a walk-in shower that was probably 36 by 36 inches with a single showerhead and a prefab wall kit. The guest bath has a tub-shower combo and a single vanity. Both do the job. Neither one feels like something you'd miss if it were replaced.

Bathroom remodeling in Sacramento CA usually starts with the primary suite. The most requested change is converting the underused soaking tub footprint into a larger walk-in shower with proper tile, a rain head, a handheld, and a frameless glass enclosure. That single change makes a bigger difference than anything else we do in a primary bath. The rest — a new double vanity, updated lighting, fresh floor tile — builds on it.

WHAT WE REGULARLY FIND BEHIND SACRAMENTO BATHROOM WALLS

Sacramento bathrooms vary too much by age to assume what is behind the tile or surround. During demolition we check the substrate, framing, and supply and drain connections before rebuilding. If moisture damage or an unsafe condition is uncovered, we show you what we found and price the corrective work before moving forward.

For a guest Sacramento bathroom remodel, the scope can stay focused: new tile, a better vanity, updated fixtures, and improved lighting. Product lead times and any repairs discovered during demolition are reflected in the project schedule rather than hidden behind a generic completion promise.

We give you a written, line-by-line estimate before we start anything. Not a ballpark. Not a "starting from" number. A real quote with every material and trade broken out. If something unexpected comes up once the walls open, we call you before we do anything about it — not after.

03
Communication is part of the work

You receive a project schedule, one point of contact, and regular updates while work is underway. When an inspection, material delivery, or approved change affects the sequence, we explain the impact rather than leaving you to guess.

Credentials you can verify

Anani Remodeling is a licensed, bonded, and insured Class B General Contractor. You can verify CSLB license #1157715 before inviting us into your home or approving a proposal.

A useful proposal should describe your project—not a generic package. We document the agreed scope, separate costs by phase, and put changes in writing so you can make informed decisions.

HOME REMODELING ROSEVILLE CA

Roseville Homes That Finally Match What You Paid For Them

Blue Oaks, Woodcreek, Junction, and Fiddyment Farm contain many planned-community homes with practical floor plans and finishes selected from a builder's package. The common Roseville conversation is not “How do we save this house?” It is “How do we make a sound house feel less generic and work better for us?”

Our approach to home remodeling in Roseville begins with those priorities. We compare the current layout with how your household cooks, stores, gathers, and gets ready each day, then build the scope around the improvements that matter. Exterior changes may also require HOA review, depending on the community and its governing documents.

Roseville has its own City Building Division and online permit process; it is not a blanket Placer County permit path. When your project requires a permit, we include City review and inspections in the plan and manage the required steps through final inspection.

Why Roseville homeowners keep recommending us
✓

✓

OUR SERVICES

Full Home Remodeling, All from One Crew

We stay focused on what we do well. Kitchens, bathrooms, additions, and full renovations. Every project gets the same attention whether it's one room or the whole house.

— 01
Kitchen Remodeling
Cabinet replacement, stone countertops, layout redesigns, new flooring, and lighting. We work around how your household actually uses the kitchen, not a floor plan from a catalog.
— 02
Bathroom Remodeling
Shower remodels, tub conversions, custom tile, vanity upgrades, and flooring. Guest bath refresh or full primary suite overhaul. Same quality of work either way.
— 03
Home Additions
Extra bedrooms, expanded living areas, ADUs, home offices. Permits, design coordination, and the full build from one point of contact.
— 04
Full Home Renovation
Multiple rooms, all trades coordinated. We map the sequence so each phase completes in the right order and nothing has to be redone.
— 05
Targeted Upgrades
One room, one system, one thing that needs fixing. Sometimes a focused scope is exactly the right call. We'll tell you honestly if that's the case.
— 06
Custom Work
Built-ins, specialty tile, custom cabinetry, and projects where the details really matter. If you have something specific in mind, tell us and we'll tell you what it actually takes.

KITCHEN REMODELING ROSEVILLE

Kitchens That Actually Catch Up to the House Around Them

A kitchen remodel in Roseville usually starts with the same list of complaints. The cabinets are that golden oak color that dates the whole room the moment you walk in. The tile countertop has a grout problem that's never going away no matter how many times it gets sealed. The lighting is a single can overhead and a fluorescent strip under the upper cabinets that flickers. The layout is fine but nothing about it feels intentional.

Kitchen remodeling in Roseville CA at its most common scope means new semi-custom cabinetry in a painted finish, quartz countertops, a proper tile or stone backsplash, and layered lighting that actually makes the room usable. Most of these projects run four to five weeks from demo to final punch list. The layout usually stays because moving the sink or the range means touching plumbing or gas, and most homeowners would rather put that budget into materials and finishes.

WHAT WE FIND IN ROSEVILLE KITCHENS FROM THE EARLY 2000S

The cabinets that went into a lot of the Woodcreek and Blue Oaks homes between 1998 and 2006 were installed fast. We frequently find runs that aren't level by more than half an inch over eight feet, upper cabinets that weren't secured to studs on every box, and plywood backs that have swelled from years of humidity near the dishwasher. Before the new cabinets go in, we level the wall and add blocking so the new work is installed the right way. It adds a day to the project. It's absolutely worth it.

When a homeowner wants to change the actual layout — open the kitchen to the dining room, add an island, relocate the sink — we handle the full scope. Structural assessment, permits, utility coordination. Kitchen remodel in Roseville CA at that level typically runs six to eight weeks. The result is a fundamentally different room, not just an updated one.

BATHROOM REMODELING ROSEVILLE

Bathrooms That Feel Like Someone Actually Designed Them

Most Roseville homes came with two and a half or three bathrooms. The primary has a double vanity, a soaking tub that nobody uses, and a walk-in shower that was probably 36 by 36 inches with a single showerhead and a prefab wall kit. The guest bath has a tub-shower combo and a single vanity. Both do the job. Neither one feels like something you'd miss if it were replaced.

Bathroom remodeling in Roseville CA usually starts with the primary suite. The most requested change is converting the underused soaking tub footprint into a larger walk-in shower with proper tile, a rain head, a handheld, and a frameless glass enclosure. That single change makes a bigger difference than anything else we do in a primary bath. The rest — a new double vanity, updated lighting, fresh floor tile — builds on it.

WHAT WE REGULARLY FIND BEHIND ROSEVILLE BATHROOM WALLS

The prefab shower units that went into Roseville tract homes in the late 1990s and early 2000s were installed directly over standard drywall. The seams on those units eventually let water in, and by the time a homeowner decides to remodel, there's usually soft drywall and some level of mold in the lower corner. We've opened up enough of these to expect it. We demo the entire surround, remove and replace the compromised substrate, apply a proper waterproofing membrane over cement board, and then tile. There's no shortcut that holds up long-term.

For a guest Roseville bathroom remodel, the scope can remain contained: new tile, a vanity with better storage, updated fixtures, and improved lighting. The written schedule accounts for selections, lead times, City inspections when required, and any approved repair work uncovered during demolition.

WHY CHOOSE US

A Bathroom and Kitchen Remodeler Roseville CA Homeowners Refer

There are a lot of contractors in the Roseville area. Here's what actually matters when someone is working inside your home for three or four weeks.

01
Builder-grade is a starting point

A functional Roseville floor plan may need better storage, lighting, durable surfaces, or a more useful primary bath—not a complete reinvention. We separate worthwhile changes from items that can stay, helping direct the budget toward the improvements you will notice every day.

02
Quotes that hold

We give you a written, line-by-line estimate before we start anything. Not a ballpark. Not a "starting from" number. A real quote with every material and trade broken out. If something unexpected comes up once the walls open, we call you before we do anything about it — not after.

03
The sequence is visible

We provide a schedule and regular progress updates, and one project contact stays accountable for coordination. If an inspection, delivery, or approved scope change affects the plan, you hear about it directly.

04
A local office and verifiable license

Our business address is 2281 Lava Ridge Ct Ste. 200, Roseville, CA 95661. Anani Remodeling is licensed, bonded, and insured under CSLB license #1157715, Class B.

Roseville projects are planned around the actual home, the homeowner's priorities, and the City's requirements. The proposal records that scope before construction begins.

Roseville and the Surrounding Sacramento Region

Roseville is part of our standard greater Sacramento service area. We also take projects in neighboring Rocklin and nearby Granite Bay, Folsom, and El Dorado Hills.

We also work back toward Sacramento and into Fair Oaks and Carmichael. The homes are different in each area. Home remodeling in Roseville on a 2003 Woodcreek tract is a different job than working on a 1968 ranch in Fair Oaks or a custom home in Granite Bay. We approach each one based on what that house actually needs, not a standard template that gets applied everywhere.

Not sure if we cover your street? Just call. We probably do.

HOME REMODELING SERVICES ROCKLIN CA

Rocklin Homes Built to Last, Finally Finished to Match

Rocklin is not one uniform tract-home market. Properties near the older downtown core can present a different remodeling puzzle from the larger, newer floor plans in Stanford Ranch, Whitney Ranch, and Surrey at Whitney Ranch. One may call for careful investigation of existing systems; another may mainly need better finishes, storage, lighting, and flow.

For home remodeling in Rocklin, we define the scope after an in-home walkthrough and a discussion of how you want the space to work. Kitchens, bathrooms, additions, and multi-room renovations each begin with measurements, existing conditions, and the decisions that must be settled before ordering or demolition.

Rocklin's Building Services division—not a blanket Placer County permitting process—handles City building plan review and inspections. When a permit is required, we plan for the City's submittal, review, and inspection steps and manage them through project closeout.

Why Rocklin homeowners keep recommending us
✓

✓

OUR SERVICES

Full Home Remodeling, All from One Crew

We stay focused on kitchens, bathrooms, additions, and full renovations, with a written scope and coordinated plan for every project.

— 01
Kitchen Remodeling
Cabinet replacement, stone countertops, layout redesigns, new flooring, and lighting. We work around how your household actually uses the kitchen, not a floor plan from a catalog.
— 02
Bathroom Remodeling
Shower remodels, tub conversions, custom tile, vanity upgrades, and flooring. Guest bath refresh or full primary suite overhaul. Same quality of work either way.
— 03
Home Additions
Extra bedrooms, expanded living areas, ADUs, home offices. Permits, design coordination, and the full build from one point of contact.
— 04
Full Home Renovation
Multiple rooms, all trades coordinated. We map the sequence so each phase completes in the right order and nothing has to be redone.
— 05
Targeted Upgrades
One room, one system, one thing that needs fixing. Sometimes a focused scope is exactly the right call. We'll tell you honestly if that's the case.
— 06
Custom Work
Built-ins, specialty tile, custom cabinetry, and projects where the details really matter. If you have something specific in mind, tell us and we'll tell you what it actually takes.

KITCHEN REMODELING ROCKLIN

Kitchens That Stop Looking Like Builder Grade

The kitchens in Rocklin's Whitney Ranch and Stanford Ranch neighborhoods have a recognizable look. Maple cabinets with a honey stain, black granite tile countertops with wide grout lines that are impossible to keep clean, a single overhead light on a dimmer, and a peninsula that's just barely wide enough to be useful. The layout is usually fine. Every single finish is ready to go.

Kitchen remodeling in Rocklin at its most common scope is a cabinet and countertop replacement with new lighting and flooring. New semi-custom or custom cabinetry in a painted finish, quartz countertops, a solid backsplash, and properly layered lighting that makes the room usable at night. Most of these projects take four to five weeks and the result is a kitchen that reads like a completely different house.

WHAT WE CONSISTENTLY FIND IN ROCKLIN KITCHENS FROM 1999 TO 2008

After old cabinetry is removed, walls and floors must be checked for level and the planned attachment points confirmed. Where support is missing or surfaces are uneven, the corrective work is documented and addressed before new cabinetry is installed.

When a homeowner wants to actually change the layout — open the kitchen to the living room, add a real island, move the sink to get a better view — we handle the full scope. That means a structural assessment, permits, utility coordination, and a realistic timeline. A kitchen remodel in Rocklin CA at that level typically runs six to eight weeks. The conversations are longer up front and the project is more involved, but the result is a room that works differently, not just one that looks different.

BATHROOM REMODELING ROCKLIN

Bathrooms That Feel Like a Finished Room, Not a Rental

Rocklin tract homes from the early 2000s typically came with two and a half or three bathrooms. The primary has a double vanity, a soaking tub that the family used maybe twice, and a walk-in shower that was built to the minimum — 36 by 36 inches, single fixed showerhead, prefab surround on three walls. The guest bathroom has a tub-shower combo and a single vanity. Everything does the job. Nothing about it feels intentional.

Bathroom remodeling in Rocklin CA at the primary-suite level often includes an early layout decision: keep the separate tub or use that footprint for a larger shower. A tiled walk-in shower with a bench, handheld fixture, and frameless glass can use the available space differently, while a new vanity, flooring, and lighting complete the room around it.

WHAT WE REGULARLY FIND BEHIND ROCKLIN BATHROOM WALLS

The three-panel prefab shower surrounds in Rocklin homes from this era were installed directly over standard drywall. The panel seams let water in over time — it's not a matter of if, it's when. By the time a homeowner decides to remodel, the drywall behind those seams is usually soft and moldy, especially in the lower corners. We've opened enough of these to build it into our standard estimate. We demo the surround completely, remove and replace all compromised substrate, apply waterproofing membrane over cement board, and then tile. There's no version of skipping that step that holds up longer than a few years.

For secondary bathrooms, a bathroom remodel in Rocklin can focus on new floor and wall tile, a vanity with more storage, and updated fixtures and lighting. The project-specific schedule reflects selections, lead times, City inspections when required, and any approved concealed-condition repairs.

WHY CHOOSE US

A Rocklin CA Home Remodeling Contractor Neighbors Refer to Neighbors

There are plenty of contractors in the area. Here's what actually matters when someone is working inside your home for three to five weeks.

01
We do not treat Rocklin as one template

The home's era, layout, visible construction, and proposed changes guide our assessment. We identify what can be confirmed before work and what may remain concealed until demolition, then put the agreed assumptions into the proposal.

02
Quotes you can actually use

We give you a written, line-by-line breakdown before we start anything. Every material, every trade, every phase is separated out. Not a range. Not a "starting from" number that triples by the time you finish. A real figure you can make decisions from. If something changes once the walls open, we call before we act.

03
Coordination has an owner

You receive a project schedule and one contact for decisions, trade coordination, and progress updates. Changes are documented, and their cost and schedule effects are discussed before the additional work begins.

04
The essentials are verifiable

Anani Remodeling is licensed, bonded, and insured. Homeowners can verify CSLB license #1157715, Class B, before reviewing a proposal or scheduling work.

A Rocklin proposal should make the scope, allowances, project phases, and permit responsibilities clear enough to compare before you sign.

AREAS WE SERVE

Rocklin and the Surrounding Sacramento Region

Rocklin is part of our standard greater Sacramento service area. We also take projects in neighboring Roseville, nearby Granite Bay, and the other listed communities.

We also work further out toward Folsom, El Dorado Hills, and back toward Sacramento through Fair Oaks and Carmichael. The homes are different in each of these areas. Home remodeling services in Rocklin CA on a 2003 Whitney Ranch tract is a different kind of project than a custom home in Granite Bay or an older craftsman in Fair Oaks. We approach each one based on what that specific house actually needs.

Not sure if we cover your area? Just call. We probably do.

EL DORADO HILLS HOME REMODELING

El Dorado Hills Homes Finished to Match What Surrounds Them

El Dorado Hills is one of the more beautiful places to own a home in Northern California. The foothills setting, the views, the mature oak trees lining the roads through the Serrano and Bass Lake communities. The homes themselves are well-positioned and decently built. Most of them were put up between 1995 and 2010, and the interiors that came standard — the kitchen finishes, the bathroom fixtures, the flooring — reflect what a production builder was willing to spend at the time. The setting deserves better than that.

For home remodeling in El Dorado Hills, the design conversation often includes how new materials read in open great rooms, how exterior changes affect a view-oriented elevation, and whether an HOA or architectural committee must review the proposal. Serrano and other governed communities may add that approval step before construction.

El Dorado Hills projects fall under El Dorado County permitting rather than the City systems used in Roseville or Rocklin. We identify the required county and community-review steps during planning, then provide a written scope and itemized quote before work begins.

Why El Dorado Hills homeowners keep recommending us
✓
County permit requirements are identified and managed when the scope requires them
✓
HOA or architectural-review needs are raised early, especially for exterior work
✓

✓

OUR SERVICES

Full Home Remodeling, All from One Crew

We stay focused on what we do well. Kitchens, bathrooms, home additions, and full renovations. Every project gets the same level of attention regardless of scope.

— 01
Kitchen Remodeling
Cabinet replacement, stone countertops, layout redesigns, flooring, and lighting. We build around how your household actually cooks and lives, not a floor plan from a catalog.
— 02
Bathroom Remodeling
Walk-in shower conversions, soaking tubs, custom tile, new vanities, frameless glass, heated floors. Primary suite overhauls and guest bath refreshes done at the same standard.
— 03
Home Additions
Guest suites, expanded primary suites, ADUs, home offices. Permits, architectural coordination, and the full build — one crew, one point of contact throughout.
— 04
Full Home Renovation
Multiple rooms, all trades coordinated. We sequence the work correctly so each phase completes before the next begins and nothing gets undone.
— 05
Targeted Upgrades
One room, one system, one thing that's been on your list for three years. A focused scope is sometimes the smartest call and we'll tell you honestly when that's the case.
— 06
Custom and Specialty Work
Built-ins, specialty stone and tile, custom cabinetry, statement kitchens. If you have a specific vision that requires a higher level of craft, that's where we're most at home.

KITCHEN REMODELING EL DORADO HILLS

Kitchens That Finally Match the Home Around Them

The kitchens we walk into most often in El Dorado Hills share a few things. Builder-grade cabinetry in a stained maple or cherry finish with pull hardware that was already dated when it was installed. Tile countertops or basic granite that came as a standard upgrade. A layout that works but doesn't feel considered. And almost universally, lighting that leaves most of the room dim and the counters in shadow.

Kitchen remodeling in El Dorado Hills CA at its most common scope is new cabinetry, new countertops in quartz or natural stone, a proper backsplash, and layered lighting that actually makes the space usable. Most of these projects run four to six weeks. The layout usually stays because the bones of EDH kitchens are generally fine — it's the finishes that need to go. When it all comes together, the room looks like it belongs in a completely different house.

WHAT WE FIND IN EL DORADO HILLS KITCHENS FROM THE LATE 1990S AND 2000S

Once old cabinetry is removed, we check walls and floors for level, confirm attachment points, and inspect accessible supply connections before the new installation begins. Any concealed damage or missing support is documented, priced, and approved before corrective work proceeds.

When a homeowner wants to change the layout itself — open the kitchen toward the great room, add an island with seating, move the range to an exterior wall for better ventilation — that's a bigger project and we handle the full scope. Structural assessment, permits, all utility coordination. Kitchen remodeling in El Dorado Hills at that level runs six to nine weeks and produces a room that functions and feels entirely different. Those are also some of our favorite projects because the transformation is hard to overstate.

BATHROOM REMODELING EL DORADO HILLS

Bathrooms Designed for How You Actually Use Them

El Dorado Hills primary suites are typically generous in size. The lot sizes and floor plans in Serrano especially tend toward larger primary baths with separate soaking tubs, walk-in showers, double vanities, and water closets. All the right elements on paper. The execution is usually the problem. The soaking tub sits unused. The walk-in shower is 36 by 36 inches with a single fixed showerhead and a prefab surround. The double vanity is builder-stock with a cultured marble top. Nothing about it matches what the footprint suggests.

Bathroom remodeling in El Dorado Hills CA at the primary-suite level starts with a practical layout question: is the separate tub staying, or should that footprint support a larger shower? A tiled walk-in shower, custom double vanity, updated lighting, and new flooring can then be designed as one coordinated room rather than a collection of builder-selected fixtures.

WHAT WE FIND BEHIND EL DORADO HILLS BATHROOM WALLS

When an older shower surround comes out, we inspect the substrate and framing rather than covering questionable material. Any moisture damage is documented and discussed before corrective work proceeds. The rebuilt assembly receives a tile-appropriate substrate and waterproofing system selected for the application.

For secondary and guest bathrooms, a bathroom remodel in El Dorado Hills is a more contained project. New floor and wall tile, an updated vanity, better lighting, new fixtures. Two to three weeks. We've done a lot of these in this area and they're consistently satisfying work — simple scope, no shortcuts, and a result that makes a functional but forgettable room into one the homeowner actually likes walking into.

WHY CHOOSE US

A Home Remodel Company El Dorado Hills Homeowners Refer

There are plenty of contractors in the area. Here's what actually makes a difference when someone is working in your home for four to six weeks.

01
The approvals are part of the plan

County permits and community architectural review are different processes. We identify which ones apply to the proposed scope, assign responsibilities, and account for those steps before setting the construction sequence.

02
Quotes that actually mean something

We give you a written, line-by-line breakdown before we start anything. Every material category, every trade, every phase is separated out so you can see exactly where the budget goes. Not a range. Not a "starting at" figure. If something changes once the walls open, we call before we act.

03
One contact keeps the details together

You receive one project contact for selections, trade coordination, inspections, and progress updates. If an approved change or outside review affects timing, we explain the impact and update the plan.

04
License and insurance are not assumptions

Anani Remodeling is a licensed, bonded, and insured Class B General Contractor. CSLB license #1157715 is available for homeowners to verify before approving work.

For El Dorado Hills work, a complete proposal should show the construction scope and the path through county and community approvals—not leave those details for after signing.

We also work back toward Sacramento through Fair Oaks and Carmichael, and further up into the foothills toward Auburn when the project calls for it. Kitchen & Interior Design Services

At Woodsman Kitchens & Floors, we believe good design starts with listening. That’s why our in-house design team works one-on-one with you to bring your vision to life, whether you're remodeling your kitchen, updating your flooring, or building your dream home from the ground up.

Since 1983, we’ve helped Northeast Florida homeowners turn inspiration into reality with timeless design, quality materials, and expert guidance that takes the stress out of the process.

Schedule a Design Consultation
What Our Design Services Include

Our design consultations are collaborative, approachable, and tailored to your needs, no pressure, just professional insight to help you make smart, beautiful decisions. We help with:

Kitchen layout & cabinetry planning

Countertop and backsplash pairing

Flooring coordination

Color and material selection

Design updates for bathrooms, laundry rooms, and more

Space planning for new builds and remodels

Whether you’re just getting started or ready to finalize your plans, our designers will guide you every step of the way—from concept to completion.

Cabinets, Countertops, and Flooring Installation
Great materials deserve great installation.

With more than 40 years of experience serving Northeast Florida, our installers work closely with our designers and fabrication team to create a seamless process and a finished space that looks and functions exactly as it should.

Start Your Remodel Now
Cabinet Installation

Cabinet installation is where design truly comes to life. Our professional installers ensure your cabinetry is level, secure, and beautifully aligned, down to the smallest detail.

We install:

Kitchen cabinets

Bathroom vanities

Built-ins and storage cabinetry

Because our installation team works hand-in-hand with our designers, every cabinet is placed exactly as planned, ensuring proper clearances, smooth door and drawer operation, and a clean, finished look that feels custom.

Countertop Installation

Our countertop installation process is precise, efficient, and carefully coordinated. With in-house fabrication, we maintain control over quality and scheduling, allowing for a smoother installation experience.

We install:

Quartz countertops

Granite countertops

Each countertop is professionally measured, fabricated, and installed to ensure a perfect fit. Our installers take extra care with seams, edges, and final placement, resulting in a polished finish that enhances both beauty and durability.

Video is not available or format is not supported. Try a different browser.

Custom Fabrication, In-House

We don’t just sell quartz, we fabricate it in-house. 

That means your countertops are measured, cut, and finished right here in Jacksonville by our expert fabrication team, ensuring a precise fit and beautiful installation every time.

Flooring Installation

A well-installed floor sets the foundation for your entire space. Our flooring installers focus on proper preparation, clean transitions, and long-term performance.

We install:

Luxury Vinyl Plank (LVP) flooring

Prefinished hardwood flooring

From layout and direction to trim and transitions, every step is handled with attention to detail to ensure your floors look great and hold up to everyday life.

Let’s Get Started
Whether you’re updating one room or planning a full remodel, Woodsman Kitchens & Floors is here to handle the details that matter most.

Schedule a design consultation or visit our Jacksonville showroom to learn more about our installation services and how we can bring your project to life.

Warm Modern Kitchen in Ponte Vedra
KitchenCountertopsCabinetsFlooring
Jan 21 
Written by The Design Team

📍 Ponte Vedra, Florida | St. Johns County | Sawgrass

Natural wood cabinetry has made a strong return in kitchen design, but today’s approach looks very different from the darker wood kitchens many people remember from past decades. Instead of heavy stains and dark finishes, many homeowners are choosing lighter wood tones that showcase the natural grain while keeping the kitchen bright and modern.

This kitchen remodel is a great example of that approach. At the center of the design are white oak cabinets finished in a soft whitewash, paired with a frameless cabinet system from the Eclipse line. The result is a kitchen that feels clean, open, and contemporary while still celebrating the natural beauty of real wood.

Let’s take a closer look at the cabinet features that make this kitchen design stand out.

Whitewashed Oak Cabinets Highlight the Beauty of Real Wood

One of the most noticeable elements in this kitchen is the use of whitewashed white oak cabinetry. White oak has become one of the most requested cabinet materials in recent years because of its durability and distinctive grain pattern.

Instead of covering that grain with a dark stain or paint, the whitewash finish softens the color of the wood while allowing the natural texture to remain visible. The finish brightens the cabinets and reduces the contrast in the grain, creating a softer and more refined look.

Whitewashed oak works particularly well in kitchens because it helps achieve several design goals at once:

It keeps the room feeling light and open

It highlights the natural character of the wood

It complements both modern and transitional styles

The finish strikes a balance between traditional stained cabinetry and painted cabinets, making it a versatile option for many homes.

Frameless Cabinets Offer a Sleek, Modern Look

This kitchen uses frameless cabinetry, sometimes referred to as European-style cabinets. Unlike traditional face-frame cabinets, frameless cabinets eliminate the front frame and attach the doors directly to the cabinet box.

This construction method provides several benefits.

First, it allows for larger cabinet openings, which makes it easier to access the interior space. Without a face frame taking up room at the front of the cabinet, homeowners get more usable storage inside.

Second, frameless cabinets create clean, consistent lines across the kitchen. The tighter spacing between doors and drawers gives the cabinetry a streamlined appearance that fits well with modern design.

For homeowners who want both functionality and a contemporary look, frameless cabinetry is often an excellent choice.

A Clean Door Style Keeps the Design Timeless

The cabinets in this kitchen use the Napa door style, which features a simple five-piece construction with a framed center panel.

The design is intentionally understated. Rather than drawing attention with elaborate detailing, the door profile stays subtle so the natural wood grain becomes the focal point.

This approach helps the kitchen feel timeless. Door styles with simple lines tend to age better because they work well with a variety of design trends over time.

Paired with the whitewashed oak finish, the Napa door style creates a cabinet design that feels both modern and classic.

Soft-Close Hardware Improves Everyday Use

While the cabinet finish and door style create the visual impact, the internal hardware plays a major role in how the kitchen performs day to day.

This kitchen includes soft-close hinges and drawer systems, which allow cabinet doors and drawers to close smoothly instead of slamming shut. The mechanism engages automatically during the final inches of movement and gently pulls the door closed.

Soft-close hardware offers several advantages:

It reduces noise in the kitchen

It prevents wear on cabinet doors and hinges

It creates a more refined, high-quality feel

Many homeowners quickly realize that this small feature makes a big difference in daily use.

Durable Drawer Construction for Long-Term Performance

Another important cabinet detail in this kitchen is the use of hardwood drawer boxes.

Drawer boxes made from hardwood are stronger and more durable than those made from particleboard or thinner materials. They are designed to hold heavier items like cookware, utensils, and kitchen tools without flexing or weakening over time.

When paired with smooth soft-close drawer slides, hardwood drawers provide reliable performance that homeowners can depend on for years.

A Kitchen Designed for Both Cooking and Gathering

The cabinet layout in this kitchen supports both function and flow. The design includes a long wall of cabinetry paired with a central island that provides additional storage and workspace.

The wall run organizes cooking elements such as the range and surrounding cabinets, while the island adds extra prep space and creates a natural gathering area.

Because the cabinets are frameless, the interior storage space is especially efficient. Larger openings allow for better use of the cabinet interiors, helping homeowners keep the kitchen organized.

A Balanced Approach to Modern Kitchen Design

Modern kitchens sometimes risk feeling cold or overly minimal. This design avoids that problem by combining sleek cabinet construction with the warmth of natural wood.

The whitewashed oak finish adds texture and character, while the frameless cabinetry keeps the overall look clean and contemporary.

The result is a kitchen that feels bright, welcoming, and thoughtfully designed.

Explore Cabinet Options in Our Showroom

If you are planning a kitchen remodel, cabinetry will likely be one of the biggest design decisions you make. The materials, construction, and finish you choose will influence both the appearance and functionality of your kitchen.

Seeing cabinet styles in person can make that decision much easier.

Visit our Jacksonville showroom to explore cabinet finishes, door styles, and layout options with the help of our design team. We will help you create a kitchen that fits your home and the way you live.

Oct 27 
Written by The Design Team

This Ponte Vedra home strikes a beautiful balance between relaxed coastal vibes and refined, custom detail. Designed and installed by our team at Woodsman Kitchens & Floors, every element was carefully selected to blend function, form, and flow across the kitchen and open living space.

In the Kitchen

At the heart of the home is a spacious and soothing kitchen anchored by custom cabinetry from Shiloh. We used their beaded inset construction for a classic, furniture-like finish, paired with the Hanover door style and sleek slab drawer fronts for a more transitional feel.

The soft blue paint you’re seeing is Shiloh’s Niebla Azul, a perfect hue for a home near the ocean—cool, calm, and sophisticated. We paired it with a custom wood range hood and floating shelves to introduce warmth and natural contrast.

To complete the space, we installed Viatera’s Calacatta Suprema quartz countertops, mitered at a dramatic 6cm thickness and cascading into a waterfall leg on the peninsula. The subtle veining plays beautifully with the cabinetry color while offering durable, easy-care performance.

In the Living Room

Just beyond the kitchen, the living room cabinetry brings in a fresh but grounded tone with Aristokraft’s Winstead door style in Maple stained Quill. These built-ins echo the warmth of the kitchen’s shelving and hood, tying the open-concept space together. 

Floating shelves mirror the kitchen’s design, offering space for display while keeping the room light and airy.

And for visual continuity, we carried the Calacatta Suprema quartz into the living room, giving both rooms a seamless sense of flow.

Designed for Real Life

From the hidden appliance garage to the beverage center and layered lighting, this project was designed with real living in mind. It’s a functional space for entertaining, relaxing, and everyday life—all while being effortlessly beautiful.

Ready to upgrade your home? 

Stop by our Jacksonville showroom today or book your FREE design consultation.

Moody Walnut & Black Kitchen in Ponte Vedra
KitchenCabinetsCountertops
Mar 25 
Written by The Design Team

There is something timeless about the combination of black and wood tones. When it is done right, it feels grounded, elevated, and warm all at the same time.

This Ponte Vedra kitchen remodel is a perfect example of how contrast and craftsmanship can come together to create a space that feels both refined and inviting. With a mix of painted cabinetry, rich walnut accents, and custom architectural details, every element was designed with intention.

A Bold Foundation with Black Inset Cabinetry

The perimeter of this kitchen features Shiloh inset cabinetry in maple, painted black, creating a strong and sophisticated foundation.

Inset cabinetry is known for its precise construction, where doors and drawers sit flush within the frame. It offers a furniture-style look that immediately elevates the space. In a darker finish like black, that detail becomes even more pronounced.

Paired with the Malibu door style, the cabinetry brings clean lines and subtle character without overwhelming the design.

Warmth Through Walnut Accents

To balance the depth of the black cabinetry, walnut elements were introduced throughout the space.

The island features a Reeded Malibu door style in walnut stained Rye, adding texture and visual interest. The reeded detail creates dimension and movement, especially when light hits the surface.

Walnut is also carried into other areas of the home, creating a cohesive flow between the kitchen and living spaces. This continuity helps the entire space feel connected rather than segmented.

Custom Arched Features That Define the Space

One of the standout elements in this project is the use of custom arches.

Above the sink, a custom-made walnut arch creates a focal point that softens the lines of the cabinetry and adds architectural interest. It draws the eye without feeling overdesigned.

In the adjacent living area, custom black arched bookcases with walnut countertops and walnut backs continue this theme. These built-ins provide both storage and display space while tying the kitchen and living room together visually.

These details are not just decorative. They give the home a sense of character that feels tailored and intentional.

Quartz Countertops That Bring It All Together

The countertops and backsplash feature Britannica Gold Warm quartz, which plays a key role in unifying the entire design.

Quartz offers durability and low maintenance, making it a practical choice for everyday use. At the same time, this particular selection introduces soft veining and warmth that complements both the black cabinetry and walnut tones.

By carrying the quartz up into a full height backsplash, the design feels seamless and elevated. It eliminates visual breaks and creates a clean, cohesive backdrop.

Designed for Both Beauty and Function

While the visual elements of this kitchen stand out, the layout and functionality are just as important.

Every cabinet, drawer, and surface was designed to support how the homeowners use their space. The island provides additional prep and storage, while the perimeter layout maintains efficiency and flow.

The result is a kitchen that not only looks striking but also works effortlessly for everyday life.

A Space That Feels Custom from Every Angle

What makes this kitchen special is how every detail works together.

The contrast between black and walnut.
The texture introduced through reeded cabinetry.
The softness of the arched features.
The warmth of the quartz.

None of these elements compete. Instead, they build on each other to create a space that feels layered, thoughtful, and complete.

Designed by Allie Reed

This project was designed by Allie Reed, whose work focuses on balancing bold design choices with practical, livable layouts.

Her approach is evident throughout this space. Every decision feels intentional, from material selection to architectural detail, resulting in a kitchen that feels both elevated and comfortable.

Thinking About Your Own Remodel?

If you are inspired by this kitchen and considering a remodel of your own, our team is here to help.

Visit our Jacksonville showroom to explore cabinetry, countertops, and design options in person. We will walk you through the process and help you create a space that reflects your style and supports your everyday life.

Woodsman Kitchens & Floors is a 100% employee-owned kitchen remodeling company based in Jacksonville, Florida, serving homeowners throughout Northeast Florida. Founded in 1983, Woodsman has completed more than 200,000 projects and has been a trusted partner for homeowners and builders for over 40 years.

About Woodsman Kitchens & Floors
Share Your Vision with Us
00:00
Play

Video is not available or format is not supported. Try a different browser.

We specialize in kitchen design, cabinet installation, quartz and granite countertops, and flooring installation.

 We are not a full-service general contractor. Our focus is on the parts of a kitchen remodel that matter most: thoughtful design, high-quality materials, precise installation, and reliable service.

What We Do

Woodsman Kitchens & Floors provides:

Kitchen design and layout planning

Cabinet installation and cabinet tear-outs

Quartz and granite countertop fabrication and installation

Flooring installation for kitchens and living spaces

We work with both homeowners and builders, offering solutions that range from cabinetry-only upgrades to complete kitchen transformations within our scope

Cabinetry, Countertops, and Craftsmanship

We install cabinetry from trusted manufacturers, including Aristokraft, Shiloh, Diamond, and Eclipse, allowing us to meet a wide range of design styles and budgets. Our countertops are quartz and granite only, and many are fabricated locally to ensure quality control and consistent lead times.

Every project is managed by experienced professionals who understand both the design and construction sides of kitchen remodeling.

Over 40 Years of Trusted Experience

Founded in Jacksonville in 1983, Woodsman has grown from a small cabinetry supplier into one of Northeast Florida’s most trusted names in custom kitchens, bathrooms, and flooring. Our showroom features full-scale vignettes and curated product lines to help you make confident decisions, from cabinets to countertops and everything in between.

We serve homeowners, builders, and designers with the same level of attention, professionalism, and craftsmanship that’s defined our business for more than four decades.

Employee-Owned Since 2023

In September 2023, Woodsman Kitchens & Floors became 100% employee-owned through an ESOP. This means the people designing, building, and installing your kitchen are also owners of the company.

Employee ownership has strengthened accountability, pride in craftsmanship, and long-term commitment to our customers. When you work with Woodsman, you work directly with people who are personally invested in doing the job right.

Learn More
Why People Choose Woodsman

Custom, Not Cookie-Cutter Every project is tailored to fit your space, style, and needs.

under one roof.

Trusted by the Trade 
Local builders and contractors rely on us for consistency and craftsmanship.

Rooted in Jacksonville 
We’ve proudly served the First Coast for over 40 years.

Serving Northeast Florida

Woodsman Kitchens & Floors serves homeowners throughout Duval County, St. Johns County, Clay County, Nassau County, Baker County, and surrounding areas, including:

Jacksonville

Ponte Vedra

Atlantic Beach

Amelia Island

Yulee

St. Augustine

Proudly Connected to Our Industry and Community

At Woodsman Kitchens & Floors, we believe strong relationships build strong businesses. As proud members of the Jacksonville Chamber of Commerce, the Northeast Florida Builders Association (NEFBA), the Florida Home Builders Association (FHBA), and the National Association of Home Builders (NAHB), we stay actively engaged in both our industry and our local community. These affiliations reflect our long-standing commitment to craftsmanship, collaboration, and supporting the growth and success of Northeast Florida’s building and remodeling professionals.

A Proven Local Partner

With decades of experience, industry recognition, and deep local roots, Woodsman Kitchens & Floors continues to be a trusted kitchen remodeling partner for Northeast Florida homeowners.

Careers at Woodsman

Join a team where craftsmanship, community, and opportunity come together.

Custom Home Renovation Experts Proudly Serving Twin Cities

At Wise Design & Remodel, we believe homes should be both beautiful and deeply personal. As a premier design-build firm based in the twin cities, we specialize in transforming homes with character into spaces that feel fresh, functional, and refined. 

Whether you’re restoring the charm of a century-old Craftsman or reimagining a more modern floor plan, our team brings together design, architecture, and construction under one roof - ensuring a seamless, collaborative experience from first sketch to final walk-through. If you value enduring craftsmanship, purposeful design, and a process grounded in trust, you’re in the right place. 

What We Do Best 

At Wise Design & Remodel, we specialize in designing and remodeling the spaces that matter most—the places where life happens. Each project begins with a thoughtful design process tailored to your home’s character and your vision for how it should feel and function. From there, our skilled team brings that vision to life with exceptional craftsmanship and attention to detail. 

What Our Clients Say 

A well-executed remodel is about more than finishes or floor plans—it’s about how you feel in your home, and how you're supported throughout the journey. At Wise Design & Remodel, we take pride in building lasting relationships with the homeowners we serve.  Our clients often tell us how much they value our thoughtful approach, clear communication, and dedication to getting every detail right. But don’t just take our word for it. 

Kitchens

More than a place to cook, your kitchen is where family gathers, conversations unfold, and everyday life begins. For a Kitchen Remodel St Paul, we design kitchens that are beautiful, efficient, and deeply personal—blending historic charm with modern convenience in every detail.

LEARN MORE
Bathrooms

Your bathroom should be a place of restoration. For your Bathroom Remodel Saint Paul, we craft spaces that elevate your daily routines with calming finishes, thoughtful storage, and spa-like functionality, whether it's a luxurious primary suite or a well-appointed powder room.

LEARN MORE
Living Spaces

From cozy dens to open-concept family rooms, our Living Spaces Remodel Services help reimagine your home’s footprint to support the way you live now. This often means improving flow, increasing natural light, or reclaiming underused square footage.

LEARN MORE
Basements

We see basements as untapped potential. Whether you envision a guest suite, home gym, or media lounge, we transform lower levels into inviting, multi-functional spaces that feel fully integrated into your home with a Basement Remodel St Paul MN.

LEARN MORE
Real Client Success Stories

Watch real homeowners share their renovation experiences—from early design meetings to final walkthroughs. 

MORE HAPPY HOMEOWNERS
Why Choose Wise Design & Remodel?

Renovating your home is a big decision. That’s why our team is built around making the process smoother, more inspiring, and more rewarding—from the first conversation to the final walkthrough. 

We’re a true design-build firm. That means architecture, interior design, project management, and skilled construction all under one roof. With Wise Design, you won’t juggle multiple vendors or worry about miscommunication between teams. Instead, you’ll work with one aligned group of experts who are focused on your goals—and deeply invested in your home. 

As one of the leading remodeling contractors in St. Paul, MN, we’re proud to offer a remodeling experience that’s as thoughtful as the spaces we create. 

What Sets Us Apart:

A Seamless Process

Tailored Design

Smart, Respectful Remodeling

A Collaborative Team

A Hands-On Showroom Experience

Your 1-Stop Design-Build Team

At the heart of Wise Design & Remodel is a small, experienced team of designers, builders, and project managers who care deeply about their craft and the people they serve. 

Every Wise Design project begins with a conversation—and often, that conversation is with founder Philip Hide. 

Phil’s approach to remodeling is rooted in decades of hands-on experience, much of it shaped by the historic homes of North London, where he grew up and launched his first remodeling business. In a city where homes were often built in the 1800s, every project required creative problem-solving, a deep respect for craftsmanship, and a sharp eye for detail. These early experiences laid the foundation for the thoughtful, heritage-minded approach that defines Wise Design today. 

After moving to Minnesota with his wife, Julianne, Phil founded Wise Design & Remodel in St. Paul to bring that same level of care and creativity to homes across the Twin Cities. He works closely with clients throughout the design-build process—offering practical insights, guiding decisions, and ensuring the final result feels both timeless and deeply personal. 

Phil believes that remodeling isn’t just about changing how a space looks. It’s about improving how it lives—while honoring everything you already love about your home. 

MEET THE TEAM
We look forward to hearing from you.

If you’re ready to reimagine your space—or just starting to explore what’s possible—we’d love to hear your ideas. Whether it’s a full kitchen renovation, a bathroom retreat, or a complete home transformation, Wise Design & Remodel is here to help you bring it to life. 

We invite you to connect with our team, visit our showroom in St. Paul, or schedule a consultation to begin your journey. 

Tell us about your project today!

Explore our client testimonials and case studies below, and see what people say about us.
Stunning Home Remodel

After relocating from New York City, Kirsten and her family purchased a classic fixer-upper with plans to transform the kitchen, mudroom, and 2.5 bathrooms including creating a seamless connection between their primary bedroom and a new ensuite bath. While other contractors encouraged them to rush the renovation before move-in, Phil offered a different approach: live in the home first to truly understand how they wanted it to function. That guidance made all the difference.

From initial inspiration to final finishes, Wise Design brought Kirsten’s vision to life with clean, respectful demolition, thoughtful product recommendations, and a full-service team that delivered craftsmanship and care at every step. “We would highly recommend Wise Design for a project like this we trusted Phil throughout the process and admire the quality of the work.”

“Whether it was a design element or architectural decision, Phil drew on all of his knowledge to guide us to the right decision with a lot of attention to detail.”

— Kristen

“Wise Design did a great job on the custom nature of this bar and the attention to detail.
We came up with a lot of really good ideas that make this a unique showpiece that everybody in my house comments on.”

— Michael

Custom Home Bar

As a cocktail enthusiast, Michael wanted a bar that was more than functional it needed to be a standout feature in his home. Tasked with transforming a compact basement corner into a fully equipped bar, the Wise Design team embraced the challenge with custom solutions and creative ingenuity. The design phase became a highlight of the process, as Michael collaborated closely with Phil and the team to craft a one-of-a-kind space tailored to his passion. Despite this being his first remodel, he was surprised at how seamless and clean the entire experience was, even while living in the home.

Wise Design delivered clever, space-saving features from a custom rollout section tailored to his liquor collection to layered lighting that highlights the stunning Patagonia granite. The result is both a functional bar and a conversation-worthy centerpiece.

Fresh, Open Kitchen

This renovation completely redefined how this young family lives and entertains. Wise Design helped turn a closed-off 100-year-old home into a bright, open space tailored for modern living. “Not only is this a new kitchen it has really transformed our entire living space on the main level.” From day one, the design process was collaborative and thorough, with Phil and the team guiding decisions while ensuring the final choices truly reflected the family’s vision.

Thoughtful design, clean workmanship, and friendly communication made the experience smooth even while the family was temporarily out of the home. The new kitchen now features a functional peninsula, custom cabinetry they love, and a layout that finally supports both daily family life and effortless entertaining.

“Not only is this a new kitchen—it has really transformed our entire living space on the main level. We have no regrets and everything is exactly the way we wanted it.”
“The staff at Wise Design are excellent. They all are very knowledgeable and professional. 
Even the contractors they used were all professional, all very friendly… made friends with my neighbors! We couldn’t ask for more.” 

— Mike & Gina

Explore this home in virtual walk through!

Full Scale Upgrades

What began as a modest kitchen renovation for Mike and Gina evolved into a full-scale upgrade that dramatically improved both form and function throughout their home. A small bump-out created space for an open, airy kitchen, while additional updates included a compact yet efficient mudroom, a stylish new powder room, and practical improvements like a new roof and gutters. Each addition was carefully integrated to enhance the home’s everyday livability without disrupting its original charm.

Our full-service design-build process made it easy to adapt as the project evolved. From custom cabinetry and hardware selections to smart layout refinements, every detail was thoughtfully considered to reflect the couple’s style and needs. The finished space is as beautiful as it is practical a cohesive blend of elegance, comfort, and smart upgrades that elevate daily life.
