*On-site build time only — excludes design, planning, and material lead times. Investment varies with size, scope, and finishes. See the full 2026 bathroom remodel cost breakdown for what drives each tier.
Our Bathroom Renovation Process

Every bathroom renovation we do in Columbus follows the same five stages, so you know what's happening and when.

1. Consultation. We walk the space, talk through how you use it and what isn't working, and get a read on your budget range before we design anything.

2. Design and selections. Layout drawings and 3D renderings, then tile, vanity, countertop, fixture, and lighting selections. You see the finished bathroom before demo starts.

3. Permits. We pull permits and schedule inspections with the right jurisdiction. Columbus, Upper Arlington, Dublin, and Worthington all run their own review process and their own timelines, and we build those into the schedule.

4. Construction. Demo, framing, rough-in plumbing and electrical, drywall, waterproofing, tile, cabinetry, countertops, paint, finish electrical, accessories, final clean. One team, one point of contact.

5. Walkthrough. We go through the space with you and close out the punch list before we call it done.

Why Columbus Homeowners Hire Elevate for Bathroom Remodeling

Choosing a bathroom remodeling contractor is mostly a question of trust. Tile and waterproofing are hidden work — you can't inspect them once they're finished, so who does them matters more than what they cost.

A decade in Central Ohio. Elevate was founded in 2016 by Michael Freed, a Columbus native and Ohio State graduate. We've been remodeling bathrooms in these neighborhoods long enough to know what's behind the walls before we open them.

Licensed and Insured. We use fully licensed, expert subcontractors and offer a 1-year workmanship warranty, in addition to the coverage provided by our subcontractors and vendors.

One team, one point of contact. Michael is on your project from the first walkthrough to the final punch list. You're not handed off to a project manager who wasn't in the design conversation.

You see it before we build it. Every bathroom includes 2D layouts and 3D renderings. You approve the finished design — and the price tied to it — before demo starts.

Bathrooms in Older Columbus Homes

Most of the bathrooms we remodel were built between the 1920s and the 1970s, and the era tells you a lot about what we'll find behind the walls.

Pre-war homes in Clintonville, Bexley, and Old Arlington usually have plaster over wood lath, cast iron waste lines, and a single small bathroom that was generous by 1928 standards. Galvanized supply lines are common and typically need replacing as part of the scope.

Post-war ranches and split-levels in Upper Arlington, Worthington, and Grandview Heights tend to have one full hall bath with a tub-shower combo, a single vanity, and almost no storage. These are the most common candidates for a tub-to-shower conversion and a double vanity.

Homes built in the 1990s and later in Dublin, Powell, and Lewis Center usually have the square footage but builder-grade finishes and awkward layouts — oversized garden tubs nobody uses, cramped shower stalls, and vanities that waste the wall.

We scope for what these homes usually hide and build contingencies into the estimate, so a surprise inside a wall doesn't turn into a surprise on your invoice.

Added Bath in Upper Arlington Basement

A full bathroom built from scratch in an unfinished Upper Arlington basement — green handmade tile, modern vanity, and brass fixtures throughout.

Basement Remodeling & Finishing in Columbus, Ohio

BASEMENT REMODELS · COLUMBUS, OH

Turn your unfinished lower level into the most-used space in your house. Design-build basement remodeling for Columbus homeowners — guest suites, home theaters, gyms, bars, offices, and full basement bathrooms, all managed by one team from design through final walkthrough.

Free Design Consult →
📱 (614) 562-0172

A remodeled basement is the most cost-effective way to add living space to your home — no addition, no new foundation, no zoning headaches. The square footage is already there; it just needs to be designed and built right. Elevate Remodeling has finished basements across Upper Arlington, Dublin, Worthington, Powell, and greater Columbus, handling everything from framing and egress windows to full basement bathrooms and wet bars under one roof.

Our Basement Remodeling Services
Complete Basement Remodels in Columbus

Turning an unfinished basement into usable living space follows a specific construction sequence — layout and design, framing, rough-in electrical and plumbing, insulation, drywall, flooring, paint, finish electrical, trim carpentry, and final clean. We pull permits, source materials, and coordinate every trade under one roof so you have a single point of contact from design through completion.

Every basement project starts with an assessment of existing conditions — ceiling height, mechanical locations, moisture history, natural light, and access points. We design around what's there and maximize every square foot, whether you're working with a standard 8-foot ceiling or a lower height that requires creative solutions.

Columbus basements come with their own set of variables. Many homes in Upper Arlington, Clintonville, and Worthington have poured concrete or block foundations from the 1950s through 1970s, and understanding how those structures behave is critical before finishing the space.

Recent Basement Remodel Projects

Elevate Remodeling designs and finishes basements across Columbus and Central Ohio. Below are a few recent basement projects — each designed, managed, and executed by our team from start to finish.

Upper Arlington Basement Remodel

This Upper Arlington basement remodel transformed an unfinished lower level into a bright, comfortable living space designed for entertaining, recreation, and everyday use. The renovation included new flooring, recessed lighting, custom trim details, upgraded insulation, and an open-concept layout that maximizes usable square footage while maintaining a clean, modern aesthetic.

Added Basement Bath to Columbus Basement

This custom basement bathroom in Columbus, Ohio transformed unused basement space into a functional and elevated extension of the home. The renovation included handcrafted green tile, brass plumbing fixtures, updated lighting, premium finishes, and a thoughtfully designed layout that maximizes comfort, storage, and everyday usability.

Upper Arlington Split Level Remodel

This Upper Arlington split level remodel updated the home with a more open layout, improved lighting, modern finishes, and cohesive design throughout the lower living spaces. Functional upgrades and timeless materials transformed the basement into a brighter, more connected environment designed for relaxing, entertaining, and everyday family use.

Finished Basement in Upper Arlington

This finished basement remodel in Upper Arlington, Ohio focused on creating a cleaner, more functional lower level with upgraded finishes and integrated storage solutions. The renovation included new carpet flooring, recessed lighting, custom trim work, and custom utility room doors designed to conceal mechanical systems while creating a polished, finished appearance.

What to Expect: Our Basement Finishing Process

1. In-Home Consultation & Assessment We walk your basement together and assess ceiling height, mechanical locations, moisture history, drain lines, and access. You'll get honest feedback on what's possible and a realistic budget range on the spot.

2. Design & 3D Renderings We design the layout around how you'll actually use the space — and around the things that can't move, like your furnace and sump pit. You'll see 3D renderings of the finished basement before we order a single stick of lumber.

3. Permits & Pre-Construction We pull permits with the city, schedule inspections, and order materials. You get a clear timeline before demo day.

4. Construction Framing, rough-ins, insulation, drywall, flooring, paint, trim, and finish work — coordinated by one team with one point of contact. Michael, the owner, is personally involved in every project.

5. Final Walkthrough We walk the finished space together, address every detail on the punch list, and hand you a basement your family will actually use.

Typical timeline: Most basement finishing projects take 6–10 weeks of construction after design and permitting, depending on scope. Projects with a bathroom or egress window run toward the longer end.

Our Whole Home Remodeling Services
Whole Home Renovations in Columbus, Ohio

A whole-home renovation brings multiple rooms and systems under one cohesive plan — rather than remodeling your kitchen this year, your bathrooms next year, and your living spaces the year after that. We design and build the entire scope as a single, coordinated project so finishes flow from room to room, trades work efficiently, and you only live through one construction timeline.

This is interior renovation of your existing home — not an addition. We work within your current footprint to reimagine layouts, update every surface and system, and create a home that looks and functions the way you need it to. Whether you're modernizing a 1960s ranch in Upper Arlington or gutting a colonial in Worthington, the scope is tailored to your home and your priorities.

Every whole-home project follows our standard design-build process: consultation, scope and proposal, design with 3D renderings, curated selections and signoff, production, and final walkthrough. The difference is scale — more rooms, more decisions, more coordination. That's where having one team managing everything from design through construction makes the biggest difference.

Open Concept Kitchen & Living Remodel

This open-concept kitchen and living remodel in Upper Arlington, Ohio transformed a closed-off first floor into a bright, connected living space. The renovation included removing multiple interior walls, installing a structural beam to create an open floor plan, and adding a functional mudroom entrance from the garage. Custom cabinetry, quartz countertops, oversized island seating, updated flooring, and recessed lighting completed the transformation.

Custom Kitchen & Bar Remodel

This custom kitchen and bar remodel in Columbus, Ohio features built-in cabinetry, floating white oak shelving, quartz countertops, brass fixtures, and handcrafted tile finishes. Designed for entertaining and everyday functionality, the renovation blends timeless materials with thoughtful storage and elevated design details.

Custom Bath Remodel in Dublin

This custom bathroom remodel in Dublin, Ohio reconfigured the original layout by swapping the locations of the shower and vanity to create a larger walk-in shower with a built-in bench and a custom 48-inch oak vanity. The renovation features large-format marble tile, a frameless glass enclosure, quartz countertops, and brushed brass fixtures throughout, creating a bright, timeless, spa-inspired space designed for everyday functionality and comfort.

Michael Freed founded Elevate Remodeling with a straightforward idea: homeowners deserve a remodeling experience built on transparency, communication, and craftsmanship — not surprises and excuses.

Michael has been in the home remodeling industry since 2012, working his way up from hands-on construction to leading full-scale design-build renovations. Today, Michael is personally involved in every Elevate project from design through final walkthrough. He leads the design process alongside each homeowner, manages trade coordination, and ensures that what was promised is what gets delivered.

Elevate Remodeling was founded as a design-build company, which means design, permitting, and construction are all handled by one team. We specialize in kitchen remodeling, bathroom remodeling, basement finishing, and whole home renovations across Columbus.

Why Upper Arlington Homes Need a Different Approach 

Upper Arlington homes have great bones. The neighborhoods are established, the architecture has character, and the lots are generous. But most of these homes were designed 50 to 80 years ago — before open-concept kitchens, spa bathrooms, and flexible living spaces became the standard.

At Elevate Remodeling, we work with Upper Arlington homeowners to bring those homes up to how families actually live today. Our kitchen and bathroom remodels and renovations are designed to feel like they belong in the house — not like an addition bolted on. We handle everything from design and material selection through permitting and construction, with one team and one point of contact throughout. 

Kitchen & Bathroom Remodeling for Upper Arlington, Ohio Homeowners
Opening Closed Floor Plans

Many Upper Arlington homes were designed with separated kitchens and compartmentalized layouts. We help homeowners create more connected living spaces through thoughtful reconfiguration and structural planning.

Expanding Kitchen Functionality

Older kitchens often lack storage, workspace, and flow. Custom cabinetry, integrated storage, and improved layouts can dramatically enhance functionality while preserving the home’s character. 

Updating Primary Bathrooms

We frequently help homeowners transform outdated bathrooms into bright, functional retreats with larger showers, custom vanities and timeless material selections.

Preserving Architectural Character 

Thoughtful remodeling should feel cohesive with the original home. We carefully balance modern functionality with architectural details that complement the existing space. 

Kitchen Remodeling in Upper Arlington

Upper Arlington kitchen remodeling starts with understanding what older homes do well — and where they fall short. Closed floor plans separate the cook from the rest of the family. Cabinets stop short of the ceiling. Counter space runs out. And the whole room feels dark despite windows that should be doing more work.

 Our kitchen remodeling in Upper Arlington projects typically address all of this — and more.

 We start by looking at the structure. Many UA kitchens can be opened to the dining room or living space by removing a non-load-bearing wall, or in some cases with a beam and post solution when structural support is needed. The result is a connected living space where the kitchen is part of the room, not separated from it.

 From there, we focus on the details that have the most impact on daily use: cabinet layout and storage, countertop material and workspace, lighting (task, ambient, and accent), and appliance placement. We work with custom and semi-custom cabinetry, quartz and natural stone countertops, and a full range of finishes, following the same design-build approach behind all of our kitchen remodeling in Columbus.

 A few things that come up often on Upper Arlington kitchen remodels:

Opening the kitchen to the living or dining area for a more connected layout

Adding an island or peninsula where there wasn't one before

Replacing dated builder cabinets with custom or semi-custom storage solutions

Installing hardwood or tile that ties the kitchen to the rest of the main floor

Upgrading to chef-grade appliances with proper ventilation

Improving natural light through window changes or lighter material selections

If you're imagining a kitchen that feels bigger, lighter, and easier to use — that's exactly what we do. Most Upper Arlington kitchen remodels take six to ten weeks from demo to final walkthrough, depending on scope. Wondering what a kitchen remodel costs in Upper Arlington, Ohio? See our 2026 Columbus Kitchen Remodel Cost Guide for a full breakdown by project type.

Bathroom Remodeling in Upper Arlington

Bathrooms in older Upper Arlington homes tend to share the same set of problems: single vanity, tub-only configuration, limited storage, and finishes that haven't aged well. These spaces were built to function — not to feel like anything. We change that, using the same design-build approach behind all of our bathroom remodeling in Columbus. 

The most common bathroom renovation we do in Upper Arlington is a primary bath transformation: swapping the tub-shower combo for a curbless walk-in shower, adding a double vanity, improving the lighting, and reworking the storage so everything has a place. The result is a bathroom that feels intentional — and that you actually want to spend time in.

 For hall baths and secondary bathrooms, we focus on efficiency and longevity: durable tile, good fixtures, updated vanities, and proper ventilation. These aren't glamour projects — they're about making the house function well for the next 20 years.

 What we handle on Upper Arlington bathroom remodels:

Converting tub-only layouts to curbless or walk-in showers

Adding or expanding double vanities with custom storage

Full tile replacement — floor, walls, and shower surround

Lighting upgrades including recessed, vanity, and accent lighting

Plumbing rough-in changes when the layout needs to shift

Heated floor installation

Frameless glass enclosures and custom shower niches

 We handle all permitting with the City of Upper Arlington and coordinate every trade — so you don't have to manage subcontractors or chase inspections. Most bathroom remodels in Upper Arlington run three to five weeks depending on the scope of the plumbing and tile work. Wondering what a project like this costs? Our bathroom remodel cost guide breaks down pricing by scope.

Basement Remodeling in Upper Arlington

Most Upper Arlington homes have a full basement, and most of them are doing very little. Storage, a workbench, maybe a treadmill. For a home built between the 1920s and 1970s, that lower level is often the single largest block of unused square footage in the house, and finishing it is the one project that adds real living space without touching the footprint or the exterior.

Our basement remodeling in Upper Arlington starts with what's actually down there. Older UA basements come with a predictable set of challenges: block or poured foundations that need moisture management before anything gets covered, ceiling heights that have to be planned around ductwork and beams, older mechanicals that may need to move, and stairs that were never meant to be a main route through the house. We assess all of it before design begins, using the same design-build approach behind all of our basement finishing in Columbus, so the finished space is dry, code-compliant, and comfortable for the long term.

From there, the design depends on how you want to use it. Some homeowners want a family room and a play area. Others want a guest suite with a full bath, a home office with real daylight, a gym, or a bar and media room. We handle the layout, the lighting plan, the finishes, and the details that make a basement feel like part of the home rather than an afterthought. If the basement is one piece of a larger project, our whole home remodeling team can plan it alongside the rest of the house.

What we typically handle on Upper Arlington basement projects:

Framing, insulation, and drywall with moisture-appropriate materials

Basement bathrooms, including new plumbing rough-ins where needed, finished to the same standard as our bathroom remodeling work upstairs

Egress window installation for bedrooms and added natural light

Custom built-ins, wet bars, and storage designed to fit the space

Recessed and layered lighting to offset low ceilings

Flooring suited to below-grade conditions, from LVP to engineered wood to tile

Relocating or concealing mechanicals to open up usable floor area

We pull all permits with the City of Upper Arlington, including the egress and electrical inspections a finished basement requires.

Upper Arlington was developed mostly between the 1920s and 1970s. That means most homes here have real architectural character — Tudor revivals and Cape Cods in older sections like Kingsdale and Old Arlington, ranch homes and split-levels in the post-war neighborhoods. 

These homes were built well, but they were designed for a different way of living. Small kitchens. Compartmentalized layouts. Single-sink bathrooms. Basements used for storage instead of living space. We've worked on these homes dozens of times and know what to expect — structurally, mechanically, and from a permitting standpoint.

Split-level kitchens are one of the most common starting points. They're often separated from the main living area and underlit. We've solved this layout many ways — sometimes with a wall removal, sometimes with a layout reconfiguration, sometimes with smarter use of the existing footprint. 

Basements are another opportunity we see in almost every UA home. A finished basement adds real, usable square footage without changing the footprint — and it's one of the better investments available to homeowners in this zip code.

REMODELING HOMES IN BEXLEY

Bexley is one of Columbus's most architecturally rich communities — with tree-lined streets, brick Colonial Revivals, Tudor homes, American Foursquares, and Craftsman-style bungalows, many dating back to the 1920s and 1930s. These homes offer incredible character, but their kitchens, bathrooms, and layouts often need thoughtful updating.

At Elevate Remodeling, we help homeowners modernize these beautiful homes through intentional design, detailed planning, and quality craftsmanship — without losing the details that make them special.

From reimagining compact kitchens to updating bathrooms with period-appropriate finishes, our remodeling approach balances timeless design with everyday livability.

We proudly serve homeowners throughout Bexley and surrounding Columbus communities.

Understanding Bexley Homes

Bexley is one of the oldest established suburbs in Columbus, and that age is written into every home on every street. The city was developed primarily between the 1910s and the 1950s, with the densest concentration of building happening in the 1920s and 1930s — which means most of the housing stock is now 80 to 100 years old. That's not a liability. It's what makes Bexley one of the most interesting places to do thoughtful remodeling work in Central Ohio.

The dominant architectural styles here are Colonial Revival, Tudor, American Foursquare, and Craftsman bungalow — each with its own structural personality and its own set of remodeling considerations. Tudor homes along Drexel Avenue and the streets surrounding Bexley's city center tend to have steep rooflines, plaster walls, and narrow original kitchens tucked toward the back of the house. Colonial Revivals throughout the neighborhood often have more formal layouts — separate dining rooms, closed-off living spaces, and kitchens that were designed for a time when cooking happened out of sight. Foursquares are some of the most rewarding to reconfigure — their boxy, stacked layout often gives us real options for opening up the main floor without compromising structural integrity.

What almost all of these homes share is a set of original details worth keeping: hardwood floors, custom millwork, built-in cabinetry, decorative tile work in original bathrooms, and masonry details that simply aren't replicated in new construction. The goal in any Bexley remodel isn't to erase that history — it's to work with it. That means matching wood tones, extending original millwork profiles, selecting tile that feels period-appropriate rather than jarring, and making decisions that will still feel right twenty years from now.

Kitchen Remodeling in Bexley, Ohio

Bexley kitchen remodeling starts with a constraint that doesn't exist in most Columbus suburbs: space. These homes weren't built with open-concept kitchens in mind — they were built with separate, functional work rooms tucked toward the back of the house, often behind a dining room and disconnected from the main living areas. That's the starting point for most of our Bexley kitchen projects, and it's where the most meaningful work happens.

The first question we ask is structural. Can the wall between the kitchen and dining room come down? In most Bexley homes, the answer is yes — sometimes cleanly, sometimes with a beam and post solution. When it works, the transformation is dramatic: a cramped galley becomes the center of the home. When the structure makes it harder, we find other ways to improve flow, storage, and light within the existing footprint.

From there the work is about materials and details that feel right for a home of this era. Custom cabinetry that extends to the ceiling. Natural stone or premium quartz that complements original hardwood floors. Hardware and fixtures that read as elevated without feeling out of place in a 1930s Colonial. Lighting that makes the space feel larger and more connected. These decisions matter more in a Bexley home than almost anywhere else — because the home has enough character that a jarring remodel stands out. That care carries through all of our kitchen remodel work in Columbus, and it matters most in homes like these.

Things that come up often on Bexley kitchen remodels:

Opening the kitchen to the dining room or main living area through wall removal or reconfiguration

Adding storage and counter workspace where older layouts fall short

Replacing dated cabinetry with custom or semi-custom built for the space

Selecting tile, stone, and finishes that complement the home's original architecture

Improving natural light through lighter material selections and under-cabinet lighting

Upgrading appliances and ventilation without disrupting the room's proportions

Wondering what a kitchen remodel costs in Bexley, Ohio? See our 2026 Columbus Kitchen Remodel Cost Guide for a full breakdown by project type.

Bathroom Remodeling in Bexley, Ohio

Bexley bathrooms are some of the most interesting spaces we work in — and some of the most varied. Original bathrooms in homes from the 1920s and 1930s often have cast iron tubs, pedestal sinks, and black-and-white hex tile that has held up remarkably well for nearly a century. Some homeowners want to preserve those details, and we can work with that — restoring what's worth keeping and updating what isn't. Others want a full transformation: a curbless shower, a double vanity, radiant floor heat, and a clean aesthetic that still feels appropriate for the era of the home. Both approaches are valid and we've done both well.

What most Bexley bathrooms have in common is limited square footage. These weren't designed as spa retreats — they were designed to fit into a house that was laid out around other priorities. The challenge is creating a bathroom that feels generous and functional within a footprint that isn't. That's where thoughtful layout planning, the right fixtures, and material selections that reflect light and add visual depth make all the difference.

What we handle on Bexley bathroom remodels:

Full bathroom renovations including demo, plumbing, tile, cabinetry, and finish work

Tub-to-shower conversions and curbless walk-in shower installations

Custom vanities sized to the space with built-in storage

Full tile replacement — floor, walls, and shower surround — including period-appropriate options

Lighting upgrades including recessed, vanity, and accent

Heated floor installation

Frameless glass enclosures and custom shower niches

Plumbing rough-in changes when the layout needs to shift

Wondering what a bathroom remodel costs in Bexley, Ohio? Our bathroom remodel cost guide breaks down pricing by scope, from preservation-focused updates to full renovations.

We handle all permitting with the City of Bexley and coordinate every trade in-house, the same way we run our bathroom remodel services in Columbus and across Central Ohio.

Kitchen & Bathroom Remodeling for Bexley, Ohio Homeowners

Improving Flow in Older Floor Plans

Formal living rooms, closed-off dining spaces, and compartmentalized layouts are common in Bexley homes. We help homeowners create more connected, functional living spaces through careful structural planning and thoughtful reconfiguration.

Reimagining Compact Kitchen Layouts

Many Bexley homes feature smaller, separated kitchens that were typical of early 20th-century design. We help homeowners reconfigure these spaces — improving storage, workspace, and flow — while keeping the remodel cohesive with the home's original architecture.

Updating Bathrooms in Historic Homes

Older bathrooms in Bexley homes often have outdated plumbing, limited storage, and small footprints. We transform these spaces into bright, functional retreats with custom vanities, larger showers, and material selections that complement the home's character.

Preserving Architectural Character

Bexley's Tudors, Colonials, and Foursquares have details worth preserving — original hardwood floors, custom millwork, plaster walls, and masonry details. Thoughtful remodeling should feel like a natural extension of the home, not a departure from it.

The city was incorporated in 1908 and developed rapidly through the 1920s and 1930s as Columbus's professional class — doctors, lawyers, and business owners — built homes within commuting distance of downtown. That heritage is still visible in the architecture, in the mature tree canopy lining streets like Roosevelt Avenue and Drexel Avenue, and in the genuine sense of neighborhood that's hard to manufacture in newer communities.

A Community That Values Its Homes

Bexley homeowners tend to have a particular relationship with their houses — they chose Bexley specifically for the architecture, the walkability, the proximity to downtown, and the community character. They're not looking to gut and flip. They're looking to invest thoughtfully in homes they plan to stay in, and they want remodeling work that honors what makes those homes worth staying in.

That orientation shapes how we approach every project here. Bexley isn't the market for fast and generic — it's the market for careful, considered, and well-executed. Material selections matter. Millwork details matter. The way a new kitchen reads against original hardwood floors matters. We plan for all of it.

Schools, Walkability, and Community

The Bexley City School District is one of the most respected in Franklin County, and the community's walkable access to Main Street — with local restaurants, coffee shops, and neighborhood retail — makes it genuinely livable in a way that most Columbus suburbs aren't. Homeowners here invest in their properties because the community around those properties gives them good reason to.

Remodeling Homes in Dublin

Dublin homes range from established neighborhoods with traditional architecture to newer master-planned communities with contemporary designs — but homeowners across the city often share similar goals: more functional kitchens, updated bathrooms, and living spaces that reflect how their families actually live today.

At Elevate Remodeling, we help homeowners thoughtfully reimagine kitchens, bathrooms, and living spaces through intentional design, detailed planning, and quality craftsmanship.

From refreshing builder-grade finishes to reconfiguring layouts for better flow, our remodeling approach balances timeless design with everyday livability.

We proudly serve homeowners throughout Dublin and surrounding Columbus communities.

Understanding Dublin Homes

Dublin is one of the largest and most geographically diverse suburban cities in Central Ohio, and that diversity shows up directly in the remodeling work we do there. Unlike Bexley or Grandview Heights — where the housing stock is relatively uniform in age and style — Dublin spans several distinct eras of development and several very different homeowner profiles. Understanding which part of Dublin a home is in tells you a lot about what the remodel will involve.

The oldest established areas of Dublin — the neighborhoods surrounding Historic Dublin Village, along High Street and the streets near the Scioto River — contain homes built from the 1960s through the 1980s. These are ranch homes, split-levels, and two-story traditionals that have been in families for decades. They have good bones, established landscaping, and mature lots, but kitchens and bathrooms that haven't been meaningfully updated since they were built. Remodeling in these neighborhoods often involves reconfiguring layouts that were designed for a different era — opening up walls between the kitchen and living space, replacing single vanities with double, adding storage where there isn't any. The work is familiar but requires careful attention to the home's original structure.

Moving further out, the large master-planned communities that define much of Dublin's growth from the late 1980s through the 2000s — neighborhoods like Muirfield Village, Ballantrae, Tartan Fields, and the communities surrounding the Dublin Athletic Club — tell a different story. These homes were built with more square footage, more formal layouts, and higher-end exterior finishes than the typical Columbus suburb. But interiors from that era have aged in consistent ways: builder-standard cabinetry, early-generation granite or Corian countertops, Jacuzzi tubs as the primary bathroom statement piece, and kitchens that were spacious but designed around a more formal, separated approach to entertaining. The remodeling here is less about reconfiguration and more about a material and design refresh — replacing what's there with something custom, cohesive, and current.

Dublin's newer developments, particularly around the Bridge Park mixed-use district and the communities continuing to grow along I-270's northwest corridor, represent a third profile entirely. These homes are newer, often more contemporary in design, and come with better standard finishes than older production builds — but homeowners in these neighborhoods are often ready to personalize spaces that still feel generic. Custom cabinetry, statement lighting, and material upgrades that reflect the homeowner's actual taste rather than a builder's defaults are the most common starting point.

Basement renovations in Dublin are among the most common projects we take on. These spaces are frequently under-finished relative to the rest of the house. Large footprints with high ceilings that are being used for storage rather than living. Given Dublin's family-oriented demographic, finished basements here commonly become rec rooms, home theaters, kids' homework areas, or full guest suites. The ceiling heights in most Dublin basements (typically 8 to 9 feet) make these genuinely versatile spaces when designed well.

Kitchen Remodeling in Dublin, Ohio

Dublin kitchens from the 1990s and 2000s share a consistent set of limitations — not because the homes were built poorly, but because production builders optimized for square footage and layout over materials and detail. The result is kitchens that are spacious by Columbus standards, often with islands and open adjacency to the family room, but finished with stock cabinetry, laminate or early-generation granite, and lighting that was never really designed at all.

The transformation we make most often in Dublin is replacing that production-built feel with something genuinely custom — and the difference is significant. Better cabinetry construction with full-extension drawers and interior details that actually function. Natural stone or quartz that was selected for the specific space rather than pulled from a builder's allowance list. A range hood that anchors the room instead of blending into the ceiling. Lighting designed in layers — task, ambient, and accent — so the kitchen works at 7am and at a dinner party. It's how we approach kitchen remodeling in Columbus on every project, regardless of scope.

We recently completed a full kitchen remodel in Bellepoint Place that's a good example of what this looks like in practice. The bones were solid — good square footage, island already in place, open to the living area. What changed was everything you see and touch: custom cabinetry to the ceiling, quartz countertops, integrated appliances, statement lighting, and a range wall that became the focal point of the main floor.

 A few things that come up consistently on Dublin kitchen remodels:

Replacing builder-standard cabinets with custom or semi-custom cabinetry built to the ceiling

Upgrading countertops from early-generation granite or laminate to natural stone or quartz

Adding a statement range hood and upgrading to chef-grade appliances with proper ventilation

Improving lighting throughout — recessed, pendant, and under-cabinet working together

Refreshing flooring to tie the kitchen to the adjacent living and dining spaces

Adding a butler's pantry or expanded storage where the layout allows

Curious what a project like this typically costs? Our 2026 Columbus kitchen remodel cost guide breaks down pricing by scope, from cosmetic refreshes to full custom builds.

Bathroom Remodeling in Dublin, Ohio

The primary bathroom in a Dublin home built in the 1990s or early 2000s almost always tells the same story: an oversized soaking tub as the centerpiece, a single or compartmentalized vanity, and a separate shower that feels like an afterthought. It was the standard luxury package of that era, and it has aged in consistent ways. The tub goes unused. The shower is too small. The vanity doesn't have enough storage. And the whole room feels dated despite being technically functional.

The most common primary bath project we do in Dublin is repurposing that tub footprint into a larger walk-in shower — typically curbless, with frameless glass, quality tile work, and a rain head or multi-function system that actually justifies the space. The square footage is already there. It just needs to be used differently. See how we handled exactly that in a recent Bellepoint Place bathroom remodel.

Beyond the shower, Dublin primary bath remodels typically include a double vanity with real storage, updated plumbing and lighting fixtures, heated floors, and a material palette — tile, stone, hardware — that feels cohesive and considered rather than builder-standard. The goal is a bathroom that functions like a private retreat and holds up to daily use without looking like it was finished from an allowance list. It's the same process our Columbus bathroom remodelers follow on every project, in Dublin and across Central Ohio.

 A few things that come up consistently on Dublin bathroom remodels:

Converting the oversized soaking tub footprint into a larger walk-in shower

Adding a double vanity with custom cabinetry and meaningful storage

Installing curbless shower entry with frameless glass enclosure

Upgrading to heated tile floors

Replacing builder fixtures with quality plumbing and lighting selections

Creating a cohesive material palette across tile, stone, and hardware

Our bathroom remodel cost guide covers pricing for projects like this, from cosmetic refreshes to full primary suite renovations.

Kitchen & Bathroom Remodeling for Dublin, Ohio Homeowners

Upgrading Builder-Grade Finishes

Many Dublin homes were built in the 1990s and 2000s with standard-grade materials that no longer reflect the homeowner's style. We help replace dated cabinetry, countertops, and fixtures with quality materials and custom details that elevate the entire space.

Expanding Kitchen Functionality

Even in newer homes, kitchens can lack the storage, workspace, and flow that families need. Custom cabinetry, integrated storage, and improved layouts can dramatically enhance functionality while creating a space designed for gathering.

Updating Primary Bathrooms

We frequently help homeowners transform outdated bathrooms into bright, functional retreats with larger showers, custom vanities, and timeless material selections that complement the home's overall aesthetic.

Personalizing Well-Built Homes

Dublin's master-planned communities feature solid construction but often lack the personal touches that make a house feel truly custom. Thoughtful remodeling adds character, warmth, and design details that reflect how your family lives.

Understanding Powell Homes

Powell's housing stock is younger and more uniform than most of the other communities we serve — the majority of homes were built between the late 1980s and the early 2010s, with the bulk of development concentrated in the 1990s and 2000s. That means the remodeling profile here is fairly consistent: well-constructed homes with solid layouts and good bones, but interiors finished to the production standards of their era, which are showing their age in predictable ways.

What distinguishes Powell from Dublin or Westerville — communities with a similar housing timeline — is the average home size and the prevalence of executive-level construction. Neighborhoods like Scioto Reserve, Wedgewood Hills, Golf Village, and The Reserve were built to a higher baseline than typical production subdivisions. Larger footprints, more substantial exterior materials, better framing — but still builder-standard interiors. The gap between the quality of the shell and the quality of the finishes is often more pronounced in Powell than anywhere else we work, and that gap is precisely where most remodeling conversations start.

Basements are one of the clearest opportunities in Powell. Most homes in the area have large, unfinished lower levels with 9-foot or better ceiling heights — well-suited for full living spaces rather than storage. The demographic here skews toward families with children and professionals who work from home, which shapes what people are building: rec rooms, home theaters, wet bars, dedicated home office spaces, and guest suites. A well-designed Powell basement adds genuine living square footage at a fraction of the per-foot cost of an addition, and in a market where buyers expect finished lower levels, it's one of the better investments available. We approach basement finishing in Columbus the same way we approach the main floor - full design, permits and one crew start to finish. 

Kitchen Remodeling in Powell, Ohio

Kitchens in Powell's executive-era homes are typically large and well-positioned, often open to the family room or adjacent to a breakfast nook. But the materials are production-grade — standard cabinetry, early-generation granite, and layouts that were designed for formal entertaining rather than the everyday gathering style most families want today.

Our Powell kitchen remodel projects typically address all of this — and more.

We start by evaluating what's working in the layout and what isn't. Many Powell kitchens have the square footage to add an island, improve the workflow triangle, or create dedicated prep and cleanup zones. In some cases, a minor reconfiguration unlocks significant functionality without a major structural change. In others, the layout is fine and the work is focused entirely on materials and design.

From there, we focus on the details that drive daily use: cabinet layout and storage, countertop material and workspace, lighting — task, ambient, and accent — and appliance placement. We work with custom and semi-custom cabinetry, quartz and natural stone countertops, and a full range of finishes so the design reflects your taste, not a builder's defaults. It’s the same standard we bring to kitchen renovations across Columbus, whatever the scope. 

A few things that come up often on Powell kitchen remodels:

Replacing production cabinetry with custom or semi-custom storage built for the space

Adding or reconfiguring an island for better workflow and gathering

Upgrading countertops to natural stone or premium quartz

Installing chef-grade appliances with proper ventilation and a statement range hood

Improving natural light through lighter material selections and under-cabinet lighting

Connecting the kitchen more fluidly to the family room or dining area

Most Powell kitchen remodels run six to ten weeks from demo to final walkthrough depending on scope and cabinet lead times. Wondering what a project like this costs? Our 2026 Columbus Kitchen Remodel Cost Guide breaks down pricing by project type.

Primary bathrooms in Powell's mid-era homes share one consistent pattern: oversized soaking tubs as the centerpiece — a design trend from the late 1990s and early 2000s that most homeowners are now ready to move past. The footprint is there. The ceiling heights are good. The bones are solid. What's missing is a design that reflects how people actually use a primary bathroom today.

For secondary bathrooms and hall baths, we focus on durability and longevity — tile that holds up, fixtures that last, and layouts that function well for whoever is using the space. That’s true of our bathroom renovations across Columbus generally, not just the showpiece projects. 

What we handle on Powell bathroom remodels:

Converting soaking tub layouts to curbless or walk-in showers

Adding or expanding double vanities with custom built-in storage

Full tile replacement — floor, walls, and shower surround

Lighting upgrades including recessed, vanity, and accent

Plumbing rough-in changes when the layout needs to shift

Heated floor installation

Frameless glass enclosures and custom shower niches

We handle all permitting with the City of Powell and coordinate every trade, so you're not managing subcontractors or chasing inspections. Most Powell bathroom remodels run three to five weeks depending on the scope of the plumbing and tile work. Wondering what a project like this costs? Our bathroom remodel cost guide breaks down pricing by scope.

The city incorporated in 1947 but saw the vast majority of its growth from the late 1980s through the 2000s, when large-scale residential development transformed what had been a small rural community into one of Central Ohio's most desirable suburban addresses. That growth was driven by several factors: proximity to Dublin's corporate corridor, access to excellent schools, large lots, and a community character that felt genuinely suburban rather than urban-adjacent.

The School District Advantage

Homeowners here tend to be in their late 30s and 40s, professionally established, and looking to make their homes work better for how their families actually live — not just how they looked in a model home in 2003.

That orientation shapes what we hear most often in Powell: homeowners who love their neighborhood, love their lot, love their school district — and are ready for an interior that matches everything else they've built. That's the remodel we're built for.

REMODELING HOMES IN GRANDVIEW HEIGHTS 

Grandview Heights is one of Columbus's original suburbs — a walkable, tree-lined community packed with early 20th-century character. From the Craftsman bungalows and American Foursquares along its residential streets to the Colonial Revivals and Cape Cods tucked throughout the neighborhood, these homes have charm that's hard to find anywhere else. But compact kitchens, small bathrooms, and closed-off layouts are the tradeoff.

At Elevate Remodeling, we help homeowners get more out of these well-loved homes through intentional design, detailed planning, and quality craftsmanship.

From maximizing storage in a small kitchen to transforming a tight bathroom into a functional retreat, our remodeling approach balances timeless design with the smart use of space.

We proudly serve homeowners throughout Grandview Heights and surrounding Columbus communities.

Understanding Grandview Heights Homes

Grandview Heights is a small city — just under 2 square miles — and almost every inch of it is residential. The housing stock was built primarily between the 1910s and the 1950s, with Craftsman bungalows, American Foursquares, Cape Cods, and modest Colonial Revivals making up the majority of homes along streets like Roxbury Road, Broadview Avenue, and the avenues running off of Grandview Avenue itself. These are well-built, well-loved homes. They're also consistently smaller than what most buyers are used to finding in the Columbus suburbs, and that constraint shapes almost every remodeling conversation we have in this neighborhood.

The average Grandview home runs somewhere between 1,000 and 1,800 square feet. That's not a lot of room to work with — which means every square foot matters, and every design decision carries more weight than it would in a larger home.

Kitchen Remodeling in Grandview Heights

Kitchens in Grandview homes are almost universally compact and separated from the main living area. In a Craftsman bungalow that usually means a galley tucked toward the back of the house, with minimal counter space, limited cabinet storage, and a layout that made sense when cooking was a solitary activity. Most of these homes were built in the 1920s and 30s, and the original kitchen was never meant to be a place anyone gathered.

The most transformative thing we can do in many of these homes is open the wall between the kitchen and the dining room. That takes a careful structural assessment — older framing behaves differently than new construction, and what's load-bearing isn't always obvious. When it works, a closed galley becomes part of a connected living space and the whole main floor feels different.

When that isn't structurally feasible, the focus shifts to making the existing footprint work as hard as it can: custom cabinetry built to the ceiling, integrated appliances, a layout that eliminates wasted steps, and lighting that makes the room read larger than it measures. Finishes are chosen to complement the home's original character rather than fight it. It's the same approach we take on every project regardless of size as kitchen remodeling contractors in Columbus.

A few things that come up often on Grandview kitchen remodels:

Opening the wall between the kitchen and dining room where the framing allows

Custom cabinetry built to the ceiling to recover vertical storage

Counter-depth or integrated appliances that don't eat floor space

Relocating the sink or range to cut wasted steps in a galley layout

Layered and under-cabinet lighting to make a small room read larger

Finish selections that complement original hardwood and trim

Timelines and costs vary depending on scope — a cosmetic refresh looks very different from a full layout change. If you're in the early planning stages, our 2026 Columbus kitchen remodel cost guide breaks down typical price ranges by project tier, so you can get a realistic sense of budget before your first consultation.

Bathroom Remodeling in Grandview Heights

Bathrooms in Grandview homes are small by any standard — often a tub, toilet, and pedestal sink in a 5x7 or 5x8 footprint. There's rarely a primary suite in the traditional sense. Most homes have one or two bathrooms shared by the whole household, built for a smaller family and a different era of daily life. That reality pushes the design conversation toward efficiency and impact. A walk-in shower in place of a tub that rarely gets used. A vanity with actual drawer storage instead of a pedestal sink. Large-format tile on the floor and walls to visually expand the room. A lighting plan that makes the space feel considerably larger than its square footage suggests. In some homes there's also room to add. We've carved second baths out of underused space — an oversized closet, a wide landing, a corner of a bedroom that wasn't doing much. It takes planning around existing plumbing runs and it isn't possible everywhere, but when it is, it changes how the whole house functions. Small-footprint work is some of the most demanding work we do as bathroom remodeling contractors in Columbus. 

What we handle on Grandview bathroom remodels: 

Tub-to-shower conversions in 5x7 and 5x8 footprints

 Custom vanities with real drawer storage, sized to the space 

Large-format tile on floor and walls to visually expand the room 

Carving out a second bath from an underused closet or landing

Recessed and vanity lighting planned for rooms with little natural light 

Pocket doors and wall-mounted fixtures where every inch counts 

Wondering what a project like this typically runs? Our bathroom remodel cost guide walks through pricing by scope, from cosmetic refreshes to full gut renovations, so you can plan with confidence before reaching out.

Kitchen & Bathroom Remodeling for Grandview Heights, Ohio Homeowners

Opening Up Smaller Floor Plans

In homes under 2,000 square feet, every wall matters. We help homeowners carefully open up floor plans to improve flow between kitchens, dining areas, and living spaces — creating a sense of openness and light while respecting the home's structure and proportions.

About Grandview Heights, Ohio

Grandview Heights is an independent city of approximately 9,000 residents located immediately west of downtown Columbus, bordered by Marble Cliff to the west and the Grandview Yard development to the south. Despite its small size — just under 2 square miles — it functions as a fully independent municipality with its own city government, school district, police department, and building department, entirely separate from the City of Columbus that surrounds it on most sides.

The city was developed in the early 20th century as a streetcar suburb, and that origin still shapes its character today. Grandview was designed for walkability before the term existed — compact lots, front porches, tree-lined streets, and a commercial corridor along Grandview Avenue that has evolved into one of the most popular stretches of restaurants, bars, and local retail in Columbus. Residents here can walk to dinner, coffee, and groceries in a way that most Columbus neighborhoods can't offer.

Who Lives Here and Why

Grandview attracts a specific kind of homeowner — typically professionals in their 30s and 40s who value urban proximity, neighborhood character, and walkability over square footage. Many are young families who chose Grandview specifically for the school district and the lifestyle, and who have invested in their homes with the intention of staying for the long run.

That long-term orientation is what tends to drive remodeling conversations in Grandview. These aren't homeowners flipping properties — they're people making thoughtful investments in homes they plan to live in for another decade or more. They want the work done right, they're willing to invest in quality materials, and they understand that in a smaller home, design decisions matter more, not less.

The Grandview Heights City School District

The Grandview Heights City School District is one of the most consistently well-regarded in Franklin County — a major draw for families and a key reason homeowners choose to stay and invest rather than move to a larger home in a neighboring suburb. The school district serves only Grandview Heights and Marble Cliff, giving it a tight, community-oriented character that resonates with the neighborhood overall.

REMODELING HOMES IN CLINTONVILLE

Clintonville is a neighborhood of neighborhoods — seven square miles of tree-lined streets, glacial ravines, and one of the most architecturally diverse housing stocks in the Columbus metro. From the Craftsman bungalows and American Foursquares of South Clintonville to the Dutch Colonials and Tudors along the ravines to the Cape Cods and ranches of Beechwold, no two blocks look quite the same. That variety is what makes Clintonville special — and it's also what makes remodeling here so rewarding.

At Elevate Remodeling, we help homeowners get more out of these character-rich homes through intentional design, detailed planning, and quality craftsmanship.

Whether you're reimagining a compact bungalow kitchen, updating a bathroom in a 1930s Tudor, or opening up a closed floor plan for better flow, our remodeling approach balances timeless design with the smart use of space.

We proudly serve homeowners throughout Clintonville and surrounding Columbus communities.

Understanding Clintonville Homes

South Clintonville — roughly everything south of North Broadway — is the oldest part of the neighborhood. Homes here were built primarily before 1930, many originally developed as streetcar communities. The architecture runs from Craftsman bungalows and American Foursquares to Sears kit homes, Tudor Revivals, and Dutch Colonials. These homes tend to sit on narrow lots with alley access, and feature original hardwood floors, built-in cabinetry, decorative woodwork, and front porches that define the streetscape. The kitchens and bathrooms are often small and largely original — full of charm but in need of thoughtful updating.

North Clintonville, stretching from North Broadway to the Overbrook Ravine, represents the neighborhood's next wave of growth from the 1920s through the late 1950s. Homes here were built as higher-end properties for the era, and they reflect the increasing role of the automobile — driveways replaced alley access, and lots grew slightly larger. Architectural styles range from late Tudors and Colonials to early midcentury ranches and Cape Cods. Many of these homes have more space to work with than their southern neighbors, but their kitchens and bathrooms are often just as dated.

Beechwold, at the northern end of Clintonville, contains the widest variety of housing in the neighborhood — from modest Cape Cod starter homes to sprawling custom builds on wooded lots. Named for the Jeffrey family's summer estate, Beechwold has a slightly more suburban feel than the rest of Clintonville while maintaining the mature trees, walkability, and neighborhood identity that draws people to the area. Homes here range from the 1930s through the 1960s, and many are ready for interior updates that match the quality of the lots and locations they sit on.

Basements across Clintonville reflect the same range as the houses above them. Pre-war homes in the south end typically have ceilings under seven feet, original block or stone walls, and mechanicals that were never placed with finished space in mind. Beechwold and the later North Clintonville builds often have more height to work with. We scope every one around what's actually there — ceiling height, moisture, and egress first — which is how we approach finished basements across Columbus generally.

Kitchen Remodeling in Clintonville, Ohio

Clintonville kitchens are some of the most rewarding — and most challenging — spaces we work in. They're compact, often separated from the rest of the home, and designed for a way of living that predates the open-concept era by several decades. The bones are good. The character is real. But the function usually needs work.

Most Clintonville kitchens sit in the back corner of the house, cut off from the dining room and living space by walls that made sense in 1928 and don't anymore. In many cases, removing or partially opening one of those walls transforms the entire main floor — not just the kitchen. We assess the structure first, determine what's load bearing, and design a solution that creates the connection you want without compromising the house.

From there, the details matter a lot in a small space. Cabinet layout has to work harder when you don't have square footage to spare. We use custom and semi-custom cabinetry built to fit the room — not pulled from a standard box size — and design storage around how you actually cook and use the space. Countertop selection, lighting, and appliance placement all get the same attention. Countertop selection, lighting, and appliance placement all get the same attention. It's the same process behind our kitchen remodel services in Columbus, at any size.

A few things that come up often on Clintonville kitchen remodels:

Opening the kitchen to the dining room or living space for better connection and light

Maximizing vertical storage with cabinets to the ceiling

Replacing original or outdated cabinets with custom-built solutions sized for the room

Adding an island or peninsula where the layout allows

Upgrading lighting — task, ambient, and under-cabinet — to make a compact room feel larger

Selecting finishes that complement the home's original woodwork and character rather than fighting it

Wondering what a project like this costs? Our 2026 Columbus Kitchen Remodel Cost Guide breaks down pricing by scope, from cosmetic refreshes to full remodels.

Bathroom Remodeling in Clintonville, Ohio

Clintonville bathrooms span nearly a century of design — from the hexagonal tile floors and pedestal sinks of a 1920s bungalow to the pastel fixtures of a 1950s Cape Cod to the builder-standard tub surrounds of a 1970s ranch. What they share is that most haven't been meaningfully updated since they were built, and most are working against the homeowner in some combination of layout, storage, and finishes.

The most common bath project we do in Clintonville is a transformation that respects the home's age without being stuck in it. That usually means replacing a tub-only configuration with a curbless walk-in shower, adding a vanity with real storage, reworking the tile, and improving the lighting. The goal is a bathroom that feels intentional and calm — without looking like it was imported from a newer subdivision.

For homes with original tile or period details worth preserving, we design around them. A green hexagonal floor, a clawfoot tub, original subway tile in good condition — these are assets, not problems. We've done bathrooms that kept meaningful original elements and still came out feeling completely current. We've done bathrooms that kept meaningful original elements and still came out feeling completely current. You can see more of our Columbus bathroom remodel work across the neighborhoods we serve.

What we handle on Clintonville bathroom remodels:

Converting tub-only or tub-shower combos to curbless or walk-in shower configurations

Adding or reconfiguring vanity storage — including custom built-in solutions for tight spaces

Full tile replacement — floor, walls, and shower surround

Lighting upgrades including recessed, vanity, and accent

Plumbing rough-in changes when the layout needs to shift

Heated floor installation

Frameless glass enclosures and custom shower niches

Preserving original period details where they add to the space

All permits for Clintonville projects are pulled through the City of Columbus Department of Building and Zoning Services. We handle all of that coordination — permitting, inspections, scheduling — so it runs in the background while you focus on the decisions that shape your home. Curious what a project like this typically costs? Our bathroom remodel cost guide covers pricing by scope.

Many Clintonville homes were built with formal parlors, closed-off dining rooms, and separated kitchens that don't match how families use their homes today. We help homeowners create more open, connected living spaces through careful structural planning — improving sightlines, natural light, and everyday function while respecting the home's proportions.

Maximizing Character-Home Kitchens

Clintonville kitchens are often compact, separated from the rest of the home, and designed for a different era. We help homeowners make the most of limited square footage through smart layout changes, custom cabinetry built for the space, and integrated storage — creating kitchens that feel open and functional while staying true to the home's character.

Transforming Vintage Bathrooms

From hexagonal tile in a 1920s bungalow to pink fixtures in a 1950s Cape Cod, Clintonville bathrooms span decades of design. We help homeowners rethink these spaces with walk-in showers, custom vanities with real storage, and material selections that make a small room feel larger and brighter — without erasing the home's personality.

Preserving Original Details

Clintonville's Craftsmans, Tudors, and Foursquares have details that newer homes simply can't replicate — original hardwood floors, built-in bookcases, decorative trim, arched doorways, and green-tiled fireplaces. Thoughtful remodeling should honor these elements while modernizing the spaces around them, so the finished result feels like an evolution, not a contradiction.

About Clintonville, Ohio

Clintonville is one of Columbus's oldest and most distinctive neighborhoods — a seven-square-mile community just north of Ohio State University that has been drawing residents since the early 1900s, when downtown residents and OSU professors began building summer homes along its wooded ravines. Over the following decades, the neighborhood filled in with streetcar-era housing, midcentury development, and the kind of mature landscaping that only comes with a hundred years of growth. Today, Clintonville is home to roughly 30,000 residents and consistently ranks among the most sought-after neighborhoods in the city.

What sets Clintonville apart is its walkability and independent identity. North High Street runs through the center of the neighborhood as a thriving commercial corridor lined with locally owned restaurants, cafes, breweries, and shops — from Katzinger's and Brassica to Clintonville Outfitters and the Wexner Center satellite gallery. The neighborhood's six glacial ravines carve through the landscape and create a park system that feels surprisingly natural for an urban community, with Whetstone Park, the Park of Roses, and Overbrook Ravine among the most popular green spaces.

Clintonville is served by Columbus City Schools, with Clinton Elementary and Indianola Informal K-8 among the most popular neighborhood schools. Families, young professionals, OSU faculty, and long-time residents all share the same sidewalks here — which is part of what gives the neighborhood its unusually strong sense of community. Annual events like the Clintonville Farmers' Market and the Fourth of July parade are fixtures, not afterthoughts.

For homeowners, Clintonville offers something rare in the Columbus market: genuine architectural character, walkable access to daily needs, and proximity to both downtown and the university — all in a neighborhood where people invest in staying rather than moving on. That makes remodeling here a natural decision and a smart long-term investment.

ABOUT US
About Your Dream Remodeling

Houston's Premier Kitchen and Bathroom Remodeling Company

Since 2010
Rated 4.9 Stars by Houston Homeowners
Best of Houzz 2023
1-Year Workmanship Warranty
Showroom and Design Center on N Fry Rd
Call 281-550-8900
Free Consultation
YOUR DREAM REMODELING

A remodel is one of the biggest investments you will ever make in your home, and the company behind it matters as much as the cabinets and countertops. Your Dream Remodeling is a full-service, design-build remodeling company based in Houston, Texas. Since 2010, we have helped homeowners across Greater Houston turn kitchen and bathroom ideas into finished rooms that look beautiful, work effortlessly, and hold up for years.

What makes us different is simple: the same company that designs your project also builds it. Design, custom cabinetry, flooring, lighting, tile, and countertops are handled by one accountable team, from the first sketch to the final walkthrough. No handoffs, no finger-pointing, no surprises halfway through your remodel.

Start with a free consultation. Call 281-550-8900 or request an appointment online.

MILESTONES:
2010
Your Dream Remodeling founded in Houston
2023
Winner, Best of Houzz Award for design and customer service
Today
Design-build team serving seven Greater Houston communities from our N Fry Rd showroom
Our Story: Built in Houston, Built on Design

Your Dream Remodeling started in 2010 with a frustration every homeowner knows: remodels that looked fine in a brochure but were never truly designed around the family living in them.

So we built the company the other way around. Design first, always. Before anyone talks about demolition, our design specialists sit with you and learn how your household actually lives: how you cook, clean, entertain, and get ready in the morning. Your must-have features, your routines, and your budget shape the plan, because in our process the most important factor is you.

That design-first approach carried us from a small Houston remodeling team to a company with its own Showroom and Design Center, where clients explore cabinet choices, fixtures, finishes, and full room displays in person. Today our team brings decades of combined professional experience in kitchen and bathroom design and construction to every project, whether it is a single cabinet installation or a complete spa-style master bathroom.

At a Glance
FOUNDED

2010

HEADQUARTERS AND SHOWROOM

1718 N Fry Rd, Suite 330, Houston, TX 77084

WHAT WE DO

Kitchen design and remodeling, bathroom remodeling, custom cabinetry, flooring, lighting, tile, countertops

Best of Houzz 2023

SERVICE AREAS

Houston, Katy, Richmond, Sugar Land, Cypress, Bellaire, Missouri City

HOURS

Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM

PHONE

281-550-8900 · 281-392-8740

What We Do

We are specialists in the two hardest-working rooms in your home. Explore our full remodeling services, or start here:

Kitchen design and kitchen remodeling

Layouts and work zones, custom and semi-custom cabinetry, quartz and stone countertops, backsplash tile, layered lighting design, and flooring, planned and priced as one system before construction begins.

Bathroom remodeling

Guest bath refreshes, spa-style master suites, walk-in showers, tub-to-shower conversions, and vanities, designed around your morning routine.

Aging-in-place and accessibility updates

Grab bars, walk-in tubs and showers, and safer layouts that let you stay in the home you love.

Custom interior renovation work

Custom cabinetry, all types of flooring, lighting, tile, and countertop replacement as standalone projects.

The Design-Build Difference

Homeowners usually meet us after hearing two other quotes: one from a designer who does not build, and one from a contractor who does not design. Here is why the combined model protects you:

Separate designer + contractor
Your Dream Remodeling (design-build)
Who is accountable?
Two companies, each able to blame the other
One team, one contract, one point of accountability
Budget accuracy
Design priced later by a builder who never saw the plans develop
Design and price developed together; fixed scope before construction
Changes mid-project
Costly, because the builder is improvising around someone else's drawings
Rare, because buildability is checked during design
Product knowledge
Designer may specify products no local team installs
Designers specify exactly what our own crews install every week
Selections
Catalogs and websites
Hands-on, at our Showroom and Design Center
How We Work: A 5-Step Process With Quality Control
1
Consultation

We meet at your home or our showroom, listen first, measure, and talk honestly about budget and possibilities.

2
Design

Our design specialists create your kitchen or bathroom plan with you, layout, materials, and finishes.

3
Selections

Cabinets, fixtures, tile, and finishes chosen in person at the showroom, guided by your designer.

4
Construction

Our own team builds precisely what the approved design specifies, with a schedule you can plan around.

5
Quality control and walkthrough

Every project runs through our documented 5-step quality control process, and we walk the finished space with you before it is called complete.

Read the full journey on our process page and see real results in our project gallery.

SHOWROOM
Visit Our Showroom and Design Center

Cabinets, stone, tile, and fixtures should be chosen with your hands, not just your eyes. Visit our Showroom and Design Center to walk full displays, compare cabinet choices side by side, and feel finishes in person while a design specialist answers your questions.

1718 N Fry Rd, Suite 330, Houston, TX 77084
(in the Energy Corridor area, serving all of Greater Houston)

Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM

Call: 281-550-8900 · 281-392-8740

Planning a visit? Call ahead and we will have a designer ready for you: 281-550-8900.

Awards, Brands We Install, and Our Warranty
Best of Houzz Award winner, 2023

read the story of our Houzz award.

Brands we install

Include Silestone and Dekton quartz and ultra-compact surfaces, Wilsonart, Schluter-Kerdi waterproofing systems, US Cabinet Depot, J&K Cabinetry and Wolf Cabinetry, and Emser and American Olean tile, each covered by its manufacturer’s product warranty.

1-year workmanship warranty

The labor behind your project is covered by our craftsmanship warranty for one year on work we perform with materials we supply. Full terms: our warranty page.

What Houston Homeowners Say

Rated 4.9 stars by homeowners across Greater Houston. One kitchen client put it this way:

angela martin
I highly recommend Your Dream Remodeling for a kitchen remodel. They recently completed a total kitchen remodel for me which included removing a load bearing wall and installing beams, new cabinets, new tile, a large island, a new pantry, all new appliances, painted the family room, installed new carpet on stairs and all new lighting, new doors. I feel like I have a NEW HOUSE ! Garret and Mike did a great job keeping me informed during the process from beginning to end. I would definitely hire them again and hope to start another project in early 2025. What I liked most is when Garret said he would have a rendering or an estimate to you by a certain date he delivered. The secret weapon of Your Dream Remodeling is contractor Luis and his master craftsmen. I have completed a lot of projects… three-bathroom remodels, house painting, hardi plank installation, new floors for upstairs, roof etc. My experience with previous contractors caused me to drag my feet on the kitchen. Luis’s team was on time everyday @ 8:30 am, professional and experts at their craft. Luis is ALL BUSINESS and he even impressed my husband which is hard to do!
Brian Tetreau
We were very happy with Your Dream Remodeling and the finished product. Garrett and his team were very professional, prompt, and easy to work throughout the entire process. It was clear that one of their primary goals was customer satisfaction. Everything from the initial project walkthrough to the final walkthrough was a great experience. Shortly after our bathroom remodel, we used them for a partial kitchen remodel as well. The results were the same…excellent! We will use them again and highly recommend them!
Chanel WEI
This is the guest bathroom, kid likes it too! Everyone works in this company are so good! They are professional, they helped cover the floor and keep the dusts away, after their work they cleaned up everything, you can really trust them!
mechteacher
Your Dream Remodeling There are good people out there that do a great job for a fair price. I needed our master bathroom remodeled to make it ADA for my wife and myself. Your Dream Remodeling, Garrett Berger and his team, did a fantastic job. The Jacuzzi tub that we were unable to get out of and a very small shower are gone and a beautiful walk-in and toilette are wheel chair accessible. They asked what we wanted and offered suggestions and did what we agreed upon. They did a Great Job!
Fred Gular
We found the workers were very considerate of our needs as they worked on the remodeling and although there were issues that arrived during the performance of their work the company and personnel worked out solutions in order to complete the project
Cynthia Wallace
Absolutely thrilled with my bathroom remodel by Your Dream Remodeling! From start to finish, the team's professionalism and attention to detail were exceptional. The design suggestions were fantastic, and the execution was perfect. The finished result exceeded my expectations - it's like stepping into a luxurious spa every time I enter. The project was completed on time without any issues. I highly recommend this company for anyone looking to transform their bathroom into a beautiful oasis!
Alan
Choosing ‘Your Dream Remodeling’ to remodel my bathroom was the best decision! From start to finish, their team was professional, courteous, and incredibly skilled. The attention to detail was impeccable, and they went above and beyond to ensure the final result was exactly what I wanted. The communication throughout the project was excellent, and they finished within the agreed timeline. I'm beyond thrilled with my new bathroom and highly recommend them for any remodeling needs. Five stars all the way!
E O
Not sure if I can say enough great things about Your Dream. I had 3 contractors come out to give me quotes and what was essentially a full home renovation. Garrett came out and really took the time to understand what we were looking for and how to balance that within our budget. His quote was fair, and the most detailed out of the other quotes I received. I knew the exact scope of the project. While the house did have some unforeseen circumstances, Garrett was always responsive and quick to provide options for us. I never felt like I was getting taken advantage of. They ended up finishing the project ahead of time and we could not be happier with how it turned out. The materials used and the workmanship is just fantastic. I would highly recommend Your Dream Remodeling.
Todd Brothers
I found Your Dream Remodeling online and wanted to get a quote. When Garrett came out I could tell he was very knowledgeable and professional and made the whole process go very smoothly. From the start to the end we have felt the quality has been very high and all the workers including Jesse and Jose have been very professional. We had our bathroom shower remodeled as our other contractor before didn't do the best job. It had some mold and some water leaking along with some damage. Garrett and his team came out, evaluated the damage and we agreed to redo the entire shower tiles and glass. They used the Schluter system which should stop all water from penetrating under the tiles. We are extremely impressed with the workmanship, quality, and design of our new shower! We will be recommending your dream or modeling to our family and friends and will probably be doing more projects with them in the future. Garrett, thanks again for making our shower beautiful and giving us the confidence that this new system will remain for a very long time
Richard Hernandez
Mr. Ike did a great job helping us locate a very specific tile for our project. His price was also unbeatable! Thank you Ike for your help.
Verified by Trustindex

KITCHEN REMODELING

The kitchen is the heart of your home. Whether you are looking for a kitchen update or full kitchen remodel, we are your one-stop shop for remodeling services. We will handle everything down to the smallest detail from concept to completion. Visit our showroom and meet with a kitchen designer or schedule a free in-home consultation.

Kitchen Remodeling

BATHROOM REMODELING

Thinking about a bathroom remodel? It may be time to remove your shower/tub combo and create the spa-inspired master bath you have always dreamed of. The bathroom remodeling services we offer at Your Dream Remodeling will transform any sized bathroom space into a functional, luxurious and tranquil retreat.

Bathroom Remodeling
